The openehr-rm validation docs for the three PARTY and PARTY_RELATIONSHIP relationship invariants now name the separate relationship container as FerroEHR’s own design against RM demographic §Party Relationships (#4531).

  • Breaking for clients that relied on the remaining commit-audit leniencies: the audit rules of the CONTRIBUTION commit now hold on every write path (#4543).

    • A description object without _type, such as {"value": "…"}, is refused with 400 on a contribution audit, a commit_audit and an attestation, and so is an attestation reason without _type. Send {"_type": "DV_TEXT", "value": "…"} or a DV_CODED_TEXT with its _type.
    • A stated empty system_id is refused with 422 on the direct writes too (openehr-audit-details: system_id="" on a create, update or delete), where the server used to replace it with its own. Leave system_id out to get the server’s, or send a non-empty one. A system_id that is not a string stays a 400 on both CONTRIBUTION routes.
    • A commit audit of type UPDATE_ATTESTATION handed to the library’s direct write calls (create_composition, update_composition, the EHR_STATUS, DIRECTORY and party writes) is refused with 400, as on the CONTRIBUTION routes. Send the audit as UPDATE_AUDIT and put each attestation in the version’s attestations list.

  • Members that NewContribution or UPDATE_AUDIT do not declare, such as a reason or is_pending on a plain audit or an extra top-level member of a contribution, are accepted and ignored: the released schemas leave both objects open (#4543).

  • The openehr-* crates take their version when they are published. A pull request that changes the crates no longer bumps their lockstep 0.0.x version: the crates publish reads crates.io, takes the next version when packaged content changed since the newest published one, and refuses to publish changed content under a version crates.io already holds. The version in the manifests on main can therefore trail the newest version on crates.io (#4555).

  • The served Web Template of an ADL 2 operational template writes the aqlPath of an ELEMENT’s value and of a data value’s parts without an [idN] predicate, since a data value carries no archetype_node_id (ADL2 master05-paths §“Relationship with W3C Xpath”). A DV_INTERVAL and its parts read …/value, …/value/lower and …/value/upper, the form the ADL 1.4 Web Template writes, where they read …/value[id6]/lower[id7] before, and the parts’ ids are lower and upper (#4559).

  • The served Web Template gives every DV_INTERVAL<T> node its lower and upper children, each of type T, also when the operational template leaves them unconstrained (RM data_types §DV_INTERVAL). Such a node had no children before. An unconstrained part carries the open inputs of its type, and its aqlPath is …/value/lower or …/value/upper. This holds for ADL 1.4 and ADL 2 templates (#4559).

  • The template example fills such an interval: an unconstrained part takes the example value of its constrained sibling, so the limits stay consistent (#4559).

  • The served Web Template of an ADL 2 operational template writes a coded input whose at-codes the template binds to a terminology as the bound terms: its code list carries each binding’s code and label and its terminology names the bound terminology (ADL2 master08-terminology_integration §“From Constraints to Concrete Codes in Data”). COMPOSITION.category bound at1 to openehr::433 reads {"value": "433", "label": "event"} with terminology: "openehr", where it read the local at1 before, and an [acN@ttttt] constraint takes the bound terms of the terminology it names. A FLAT or STRUCTURED composition without a category, and the example composition, now carry openehr::433. The aqlPath of every data value drops its [idN] predicate, so a constrained category and context/setting read /category and /context/setting (#4574).

  • A CONTRIBUTION’s versions[] entry records its merge inputs: the other_input_version_uids it states are stored on the committed ORIGINAL_VERSION and served on every read, where the server used to refuse the member with 400. The uids may name versions the server does not hold; an empty list or an entry that is not an OBJECT_VERSION_ID is a 422 (#4577).

  • Other members UPDATE_VERSION does not declare, such as item or an extension member, are accepted and ignored, where the server used to refuse them with 400: the released schema leaves the object open, as it does NewContribution and UPDATE_AUDIT. A uid or contribution on a version entry is still refused with 400, because the server assigns both, and so is a _type other than UPDATE_VERSION or ORIGINAL_VERSION (#4577).

  • The admin dump route’s refusals name its parameters by their wire names and list the accepted values, not the Service Model class names. A bad logical_format or compression_format now reads “<field> must be a string, one of …” or “<field> names no accepted value: … (expected one of …)”, and a non-integer segment_split_size reads “segment_split_size must be an integer size in kb”. The served OpenAPI text for the route no longer names EXPORT_SPEC or EXPORT_FORMAT (#4634).

  • Five archive dump and load failures still answer 500, and their bodies are now fixed text that echoes no value from the archive: (#4657)

    • an unreadable data segment no longer names the segment, though manifest.json and demographic-commons.json are still named;
    • an unknown logical format in the manifest no longer echoes the declared value;
    • a version whose id carries a path separator, and a version whose commit audit the export lacks, no longer name the version.

  • A failed expansion of a party’s protected national identifiers still answers 500, and its body now reads “expanding the protected identifiers of a party version failed” without echoing the requested version uid: a 500 body carries curated text only (#4657).

  • Two query failures still answer 500, and their bodies now carry curated text only. A stored query whose record holds no query text reads “the stored query has no query text” without echoing its name, and a terminology server failure while a TERMINOLOGY('expand', …) operand is resolved reads “the terminology service failed while the query was being planned” instead of the upstream message (#4657).

  • The db_transactions counter (outcome="commit") now counts every committed single-object write. It used to leave out EHR_STATUS and DIRECTORY writes (#4659).

  • OPTIONS on the API base path sends conformance_profile as BASE+OPTIONS where it sent STANDARD. The build derives the value from the committed Veredictum record, docs/conformance/ferroehr/summary.md: BASE+OPTIONS when the BASE rows and the run OPTIONS rows have none failed and none errored, BASE when only the BASE rows do, and the member left out otherwise. ITS-REST 1.1.0 types the member as a free string and CNF names no profiles, so the values are FerroEHR’s own. The [rest.identity] conformance_profile configuration key is removed: a configuration that still sets it is refused at boot as an unknown key (#4672).

  • The viewer answers every request other than GET and HEAD that arrives without a session, to any path but the sign-in page, the OIDC routes, sign-out and the search answer, with the sign-in page that says the session ended, before any handler runs. A post to a page returns there after signing in; a post to the export, preference, sidebar or paging route returns to the dashboard. The export post used to answer 303 to /login, and the preference, sidebar and paging posts ran without a session (#4724).

  • The conformance instrument is Veredictum 0.4.0, and the published conformance record (docs/conformance/ferroehr/results.json with its summary.md) is a 0.4.0 released-profile run. The party statement answers the 0.4.0 catalogue: it keeps the xml-namespace-v2 arm, which now asks only whether the TRIAL http://schemas.openehr.org/v2 namespace is also accepted, and selects the new development-profile option arm adl2-id-coded-supported (#4771).

Removed

  • The conformance pipeline no longer runs EHRbase or the extra FerroEHR deployments. docker/sut-ehrbase.yml, the EHRbase record and party set, docs/conformance/COMPARISON.md, the book’s Comparison with EHRbase page, and the openPGP-signing, fail-open and stable-spec compose overlays (docker/sut-signing-pgp.yml, sut-pgp-parallel.yml, sut-terminology-failclosed.yml, sut-terminology-failopen.yml, sut-spec-stable.yml) with the test signing keys under corpus/keys/ are gone. scripts/conformance.sh no longer takes CONF_SUT, CONF_IXIT or CONF_STATEMENT, and refuses CONF_PERF_CLASS and CONF_STRESS until the measured lanes move to the Veredictum perf/ tree (#4448).

  • The Veredictum pin watcher workflow, scripts/checks/veredictum-pin.sh with its veredictum-pin-guard job, and the no-conformance-run label are gone: a pin bump now runs the new catalogue against its own build in the Conformance workflow (#4449).

  • The Veredictum 0.1.6 conformance documents: CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md, CONFORMANCE_STATEMENT.md, CONFORMANCE_CERTIFICATE.md, verdicts.json, run-exceptions.json, the CORE, STANDARD, OPTIONS, SEC-BASIC and performance badge files, and the heat grid and chapter bars the book and the landing page drew from them (#4451).

  • The CONF_PERF_CLASS, CONF_PERF_HOURS and CONF_STRESS settings of the measured lanes are gone, along with the class runs, the step-load stress ladder and the AQL probe, which Veredictum 0.3.1 removed (#4452).

  • The separate SMART step of the Conformance workflow, the smart stage of scripts/conformance.sh with its CONF_SMART_OUT, and docs/conformance/party/ferroehr/ixit-smart.json are gone: the one catalogue run covers the SMART documents. The party statement no longer carries the performance block, which the Veredictum 0.3.1 statement schema refuses (#4503).

  • The empty linkage storage domain is gone: its schema, its ferroehr_linkage role, the [storage.linkage] and [storage.migrate.linkage] configuration tables, its pool, the database.linkage and backup.linkage chart values, the ferroehr-backup-linkage compose job and the btree_gist extension only its table needed. A configuration that still sets [storage.linkage] or [storage.migrate.linkage] is refused at boot as an unknown key. Cohort and AQL demographic join crossings still write their linkage-domain access records. Upgrade note: remove those keys and values before you upgrade. On a co-located database, migration audit/0021_drop_linkage_domain.sql drops the schema, the role and the extension at the first boot, and raises a NOTICE for any of them it cannot drop. When the linkage domain lived in a database of its own, [storage.audit] names another database, or the cluster holds more than one FerroEHR database, run in each such database, as a superuser or a member of ferroehr_linkage: DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS linkage CASCADE; REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA ext FROM ferroehr_linkage; REVOKE ALL ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA ext FROM ferroehr_linkage; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA ext REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM ferroehr_linkage; DROP OWNED BY ferroehr_linkage; DROP EXTENSION IF EXISTS btree_gist; then DROP ROLE ferroehr_linkage; once per cluster. The released grant files still name ferroehr_linkage, so a first install whose migrator holds no CREATEROLE still provisions that role and drops it after the first boot (#4684).

  • A party migration drops the database function party.resolve_national_identifier. No server path has called it since the linkage domain was removed (#4697).

  • The viewer no longer reads LEPTOS_SITE_ADDR: a value naming another address than server.listen no longer refuses the start. server.listen (FERROEHR_VIEWER__SERVER__LISTEN) sets the listen address (#4725).

Fixed

  • The hosted sandbox seeds its full demo dataset again. The v5.5.0 reseed stopped at the ADL 2 archetype library (233 stored / 89 refused against the pinned 231 / 91) because the box’s .env still forced FerroTERM 0.1.6, which reads none of the FerroTERM 0.3 settings the sandbox posture passes, so it served no LOINC and VETDF could only warn on braden_scale’s mistyped LA9605-4. The corpus, the pin and the CDR were right. The seed now asks the CDR for a LOINC code before the library step and names a posture without LOINC (SANDBOX_TERMINOLOGY=without-loinc opts a local run into 233 / 89), checks that the two files it names move together, and a corpus test holds the manifest’s pin to the adjudicated split with and without LOINC. The FerroPIX rollout script retires a stale FERROTERM_IMAGE override, checks that FerroTERM runs the pinned version and serves LOINC, and wipes before it seeds over an unfinished seed (#4278).

  • The measurement overlay docker/sut-measurement.yml switches the caller rate limiter off by removing the [server.caller_rate] keys, so the server logs caller rate limiting configured with enabled=false at boot, instead of setting a rate of 4294967295 per second that ferrohealth-server 0.3.5 truncated to a zero interval and that answered stray 429s under concurrency. scripts/conformance.sh refuses to start a measurement stack whose ferroehr service still sets a caller rate (#4281).

  • A response to a request whose body FerroEHR left unread, such as a 404 to a POST of a path it does not serve or a declared-length 413, now carries Connection: close. The connection closed after such a response without saying so, and a client that sent its next request on it met a closed socket, which a non-idempotent request cannot safely retry (RFC 9112 §9.6) (#4283).

  • A [server.caller_rate] above 1 000 000 000 requests per second no longer answers 429 to concurrent requests: such a rate now limits nothing, as its operator meant (#4283).

  • Every request leaves one request line, a timeout 408, a declared-length 413 and the 500 of a panicked handler included, and a 413 for a body with no declared length that passes [server] body_limit_bytes is answered with the openEHR error body, as the declared-length 413 is (#4283).

  • An AQL query whose WHERE clause chains thousands of NOT, AND or OR terms no longer overflows the stack and aborts the server. The parser refuses a query that nests brackets and CONTAINS deeper than 64 levels or builds an expression deeper than 512 levels with 400 Bad Request, before any recursive pass runs, on the ad-hoc, stored-query store and execution paths alike. A long OR over one path is written as MATCHES {…}, which the bound does not count. A statement PostgreSQL refuses for its own complexity limit (SQLSTATE class 54) also answers 400 instead of 500. openehr-query gains ParseError::TooDeep (#4284).

  • An AQL query (ad hoc or stored) whose client disconnects, or that the server’s own query.timeout_ms or HTTP request timeout gives up on, no longer keeps its statement running and its pooled connection busy until the statement ends. The connection is closed instead of returned to the pool, so the slot frees at once, and every pooled session now sets PostgreSQL’s client_connection_check_interval to one second, so the backend stops the abandoned statement within about a second. The composition-count statistics behave the same way (#4285).

  • The server’s resident memory no longer climbs under sustained load until the container’s memory limit kills it. The ferroehr binary now allocates through mimalloc instead of glibc malloc, whose per-thread arenas kept freed memory and never gave it back. On a load test of 10 000 mixed jobs at 48 workers the peak resident set fell from 2.3 to 3.2 GB (growing run after run) to about 600 MB, and throughput rose by about a third (#4288).

  • A request whose database connection a PostgreSQL restart, a crash or the network cuts now answers 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After, as a request that cannot get a connection already did, instead of 500. SQLSTATE class 08 (except 08P01), 57P01, 57P02, 57P03 and 57P05, and a reset, aborted or closed socket on an open session count as such a cut (#4290).

  • While PostgreSQL is down, requests that need the database answer 503 with Retry-After about a second after the first one starts waiting, and at once after that, instead of each queueing up to db.acquire_timeout_secs (30 seconds by default). An acquire that has waited a second tries one connection of its own; when that cannot reach the database, the outage is known until a fresh attempt connects, and requests are served again as soon as one does. A pool that is only busy keeps queueing as before (#4323).

  • Superseding a composition or a party no longer slows down as its history grows. The foreign-key check that every new node and attestation row makes against its version could scan all versions of the object instead of probing one, depending on the planner statistics at the time: on the storage bench, superseding an object with a few hundred versions took about 14 ms instead of 9 ms when the plan flipped. Migrations clinical/0022 and party/0013 re-key the version-tree uniqueness constraint uq_version_tree with the object id last, so the check always probes the primary key. The constraint enforces the same uniqueness as before (#4340).

  • The FHIR rendering of an access record ehds-logging does not classify (a template upload, a stored-query write, a template read) now carries the IHE BALP 1.1.4 entity:data slice its Create, Read, Update or Delete profile requires: type 2, role 4 and what.identifier, naming the operation when the record names no object. HAPI FHIR’s validator refused the template upload record without it (#4353).

  • A + in a query string is a literal plus, as RFC 3986 §2.1 and §3.4 decode a URI query, on every ITS-REST operation and every extension route: a date-time offset such as 2026-10-28T10:00:00+01:00 or an AQL parameter sent with an unencoded + reaches the server unchanged, where it was read as a space. A space in a query value is sent as %20. This reverses the form-decoding of #3891: a client that writes a space as + now sends a plus. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.114 (#4356).

  • An AQL EHR e[ehr_id/value='…'] predicate whose value is not a UUID ('1234', the AQL 1.1.0 example) answers an empty result, as its WHERE e/ehr_id/value = '…' spelling does, on POST and GET /query/aql; it was refused with 400. Both spellings lower the EHR id comparison through one path, and a value the database cannot cast is refused with a message that no longer claims it came from a query parameter (#4378).

  • A request sent on a kept-alive connection that sat idle longer than [server] header_read_timeout_ms (30 s by default) is answered. The server used to close such a connection, sometimes while the request was arriving, so a client that reused it got EOF with no answer and no server log line, and a client that never retries a POST on a reused connection, such as Go’s net/http, reported a composition commit as failed. An idle connection now stays open until [server] idle_timeout_ms (120 s by default) and then ends cleanly before any new request byte; keep that limit longer than the idle timeout of your clients (90 s for Go) and of any load balancer in front (#4381).

  • An AQL query with an archetype predicate no longer builds the archetype index bitmap of the whole store once per version. The planner multiplied the selectivities of the archetype columns, which each archetype fixes together, and expected about 15 000 of 545 067 blood-pressure OBSERVATIONs; a query over one EHR then took 38.8 s and answered 408. Clinical migration 0021_archetype_statistics.sql gives the columns a statistics object, and the same query takes 0.3 s (#4399).

  • FROM PERSON p CONTAINS EHR e (and the ORGANISATION and ROLE roots) joins a party to the EHR whose EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref names it, so a party created with POST /demographic/person and an EHR created with POST /ehr answer their row with no other call. Before, the join read only the party-to-EHR map, which no REST route writes, and answered no rows on a deployed server. The reference matches when its id.value is the party’s uid without ::<system>::<version> and its type is the root class or its RM ancestor (ACTOR, PARTY), in any namespace; an EHR linked both ways answers once (#4411).

  • An AQL projection whose path ends on a list attribute inside a node’s data (c/feeder_audit/originating_system_item_ids, c/links, c/context/participations, c/composer/identifiers, .../mappings) answers the list itself, [{…}, {…}], and null when the list is absent. It answered the list wrapped in a second list, [[{…}, {…}]]; a client that unwrapped that outer array reads the column directly now. A path that continues below a list (.../originating_system_item_ids/id) still answers the array of its matches, ["…", "…"]. COUNT over a path ending on a list counts its elements (#4413).

  • Reading one version of a composition, EHR_STATUS, folder or party by its version id no longer slows down as the object’s history grows. Once a connection reused its prepared read, the plan scanned every version of the object and kept the one asked for: on the storage bench’s history of 500 versions such a read touched about 520 buffers instead of 12 to 24. Migrations clinical/0023 and party/0014 add an index on the version tree id columns of both storage tiers, so the read probes the one version it returns (#4420).

  • An audit store that 5.6.0-rc2 migrated starts again. Audit migration 0017 changed after 5.6.0-rc2 shipped it, so the server refused such a store on the migration’s checksum at boot. 0017 is back to its 5.6.0-rc2 text, and the new audit migration 0019_search_tokens_pending_list.sql gives the search token index its pending list of 512 kB, so a store that 5.6.0-rc2 migrated upgrades in place (#4424).

  • An AQL query ordered by c/uid/value with a LIMIT no longer starts a parallel worker on every call, and no longer switches between that plan and a sort of the whole join depending on the planner statistics. The version uid it sorts on had no index, so the planner sorted the version rows through a parallel Gather Merge, which costs a worker’s start-up per query on a server of any size: about 19 ms on the storage bench’s CI runner, where the two flat-shape path reads measured 23 ms in some rounds and 42 ms in others. Migrations clinical/0024 and party/0015 add an index on the uid expression of the hot version partition, so the query reads versions in uid order from it in one backend and stops at the limit (#4429).

  • An AQL query that reads values along a path no longer spends up to a second compiling itself before it runs. Each path step was bound through a set-returning function that PostgreSQL estimates at ten rows, so a chain of steps multiplied the row estimate tenfold per step: the planner chose join orders for a statement millions of times larger than the real one and switched on JIT compilation for it. On the storage bench, a wide projection of 9 values over one EHR read in 1 s instead of 15 to 20 ms, and an ordered WHERE on a magnitude in about 0.5 s instead of 50 ms (#4430). Each step is now a LATERAL subquery that the planner estimates from its own plan; results do not change (#4431).

  • An AQL lookup by an ELEMENT value, such as a person by an identifier (WHERE id/items[at0001]/value/id = $v) or a composition by a text value, read every node of the archetype in both stores and tested the value last: about 350 ms at 50 000 persons. The engine now anchors such an equality on the ELEMENT rows of the same version by their search text (ext.node_search_text, ext migration 0006), which the new partial expression index idx_node_hot_value_search and its statistics object serve (clinical migration 0025, party migration 0016), so the lookup reads the one object: 26 buffers and under a millisecond at 50 000 persons. The party store also gets the archetype dependency statistics the clinical store has had since 5.6.0-rc2 (party migration 0017). The storage bench measures the lookup as person_identifier_lookup (#4437).

  • The revision history and every point read of a version now reach the version’s commit audit through a lateral subquery that probes pk_commit_audit by key once per version row, so stale statistics on the partitioned version table can no longer turn the read into a walk of the whole commit audit index (1 318 buffers against 21 for a four-version object beside 1 300 others) (#4438).

  • A revision history or a current-version read of a COMPOSITION committed after the partitioned version table last had statistics could walk the whole commit audit index: the planner held the highest commit audit id of the seed for the highest there is and rated a merge join over pk_commit_audit as cheap. On a store of 1 300 compositions the history of a four-version object read 1 318 buffers instead of 21, and the storage bench read revision_history at about 440 buffers per call in 3 of 8 rounds. The server now keeps the partitioned parents’ statistics (#4453), and each read probes the commit audit by key (#4438).

  • An AQL lookup of an EHR by the subject of its EHR_STATUS (WHERE e/ehr_status/subject/external_ref/id/value = $u AND e/ehr_status/subject/external_ref/namespace = $n) joined every EHR_STATUS version and read the subject out of its stored fragment: about 150 ms on a store of a few thousand EHRs. The two leaves now read the EHR row’s subject_id and subject_namespace, the copy the commit keeps of the current EHR_STATUS subject, so the lookup enters through uq_ehr_subject and reads one row. The storage bench measures it as ehr_by_subject (#4442).

  • The partitioned tables node, version and vo_attestation of the clinical and party stores never had planner statistics of their own, since autovacuum does not analyze a partitioned table, so the planner estimated joins over them without any (PostgreSQL 18 §24.1.3). The server now runs ANALYZE ONLY on them, and on ehr while autovacuum has never analyzed it, after applying the migrations, after load_ehrs, at boot and every hour. The role it runs as needs the MAINTAIN privilege on those tables; without it the server logs the tables it could not analyze. The population CONTAINS of an archetype now enters through idx_node_hot_arch_subsume (3 703 buffers to 1 745 on the storage bench’s seed) (#4453).

  • A party delete (DELETE /demographic/{agent,group,organisation,person,role}/{uid_based_id}) and the party relationship delete now answer 400 when the path names the versioned object instead of its latest OBJECT_VERSION_ID, and delete nothing. They answered 204 and deleted the current version. The release requires the preceding_version_uid in that path (ITS-REST agent_delete.yaml and its four siblings) (#4478) (#4458).

  • A CONTRIBUTION member outside the operation’s member set, a party in an EHR CONTRIBUTION or a FOLDER in a demographic CONTRIBUTION, now answers 400 as a body that fails the request schema. It answered 422 (#4459).

  • A party update whose body carries no uid now checks each relationship source against the party the path names and refuses a foreign source with 422, as RM Relationships_validity requires. The check ran only when the body carried a uid, so such an update committed a relationship sourced at another party (#4460).

  • An ADL 1.4 template upload whose XML ends with an element still open now answers 400, as for any document that is not well-formed XML. The well-formedness gate stopped at the end of input without checking that every element was closed, so a truncated upload answered 422 (#4461).

  • A canonical JSON body that the published ITS-JSON schema admits and the RM refuses, such as a DV_URI or DV_EHR_URI without value or a DV_INTERVAL limit DV_ORDINAL without symbol, now answers 422 naming the member, on the direct commit routes, the CONTRIBUTION members and the party commits. A body the schema refuses still answers 400. All of them answered 400 (#4463).

  • A directory create or update whose root FOLDER names an archetype in archetype_node_id and carries no archetype_details now answers 422 and commits nothing: an archetype root carries archetype_details (RM common §The LOCATABLE Class). FerroEHR created such a directory. A 553|incomplete| commit and a nested FOLDER keep it optional. The viewer’s empty directory root now carries archetype_details (#4464).

  • AQL EHR e NOT CONTAINS <class expression> now runs and returns the EHRs that hold no matching object. It was refused as unsupported with 400 (#4465).

  • An AQL comparison between a DV_DATE_TIME path that ends on the data value itself, such as c/context/start_time, and a date-time literal now compares the instants both name, so values with different offsets compare correctly. The comparison read the whole data value and matched nothing (#4466).

  • A container member whose node id names an object constraint of the template but whose RM type conforms to none of them, such as an ELEMENT where the template allows only a CLUSTER, is now refused with 422. Only the opposite direction was refused (#4468).

  • An ADL 1.4 template upload with Prefer: return=representation now answers the representation Accept names: the OPT XML, or the Web Template under application/openehr.wt+json or application/json. An Accept outside those answers 406 and stores nothing. The upload always answered XML (#4469).

  • A Simplified Format COMPOSITION commit without the openehr-template-id header, and a flat |raw value without _type, now answer 400. Both answered 422 (#4470).

  • A Simplified Flat or Structured …/action_archetype_id now sets the String ACTIVITY.action_archetype_id, and the flat output writes it back. The converter built an object from the template’s string constraint, so the commit answered 422 (#4471).

  • ctx/action_ism_transition_current_state, as a rubric or a code, now sets ACTION.ism_transition.current_state of every ACTION the document gives no state. The converter wrote 524|initial| first and the context value never applied (#4472).

  • ctx/instruction_narrative now becomes INSTRUCTION.narrative of every INSTRUCTION the document gives no narrative. A placeholder <narrative> was stored instead (#4473).

  • The Simplified Flat DV_INTERVAL suffixes |lower_unbounded, |upper_unbounded, |lower_included and |upper_included are now read on an interval whose bounds are template nodes, and the flat output writes an unbounded flag when true and an included flag when false. The suffixes were refused as unknown with 422 (#4474).

  • An AQL query aimed at named EHRs (the ITS-REST ehr_id parameter) reads those EHRs’ objects first and each object’s own content after them, whatever the planner statistics say. When an archetype’s rows fell out of the most-common-value list of the archetype statistics, the planner estimated them at one row and could start from that archetype over the whole population, evaluating every projected path for every EHR’s rows before the EHR filter: the storage bench’s wide projection over one EHR read about 10 000 pages per call in some rounds and 1 200 in others. A node contained in a versioned object is now read inside its parent on such a query; results do not change (#4487).

  • AQL TERMINOLOGY('expand', …) against a FHIR terminology server takes the value set from the url argument when params_uri is the $expand query form (url=http://…), as the openEHR AQL examples write it, and still takes a bare value-set URL as it is. A query form without url is a 400 that names the missing argument. Before, the whole params_uri went to the server as the URL, and the query was answered 400 because the value set was not found (#4488).

  • AQL TERMINOLOGY('validate', …) and TERMINOLOGY('subsumes', …) keep a params_uri argument whole when its value carries a ?, as the QUERY master03 example url=http://snomed.info/sct?fhir_vs does. Before, the arguments were read from after the first ? anywhere in params_uri, so the value-set URL reached the terminology server truncated and the arguments before it were lost. A params_uri that starts with a path still has its arguments read from after the path’s ? (#4490).

  • An ADL 2 template whose constituent archetype the CDR does not hold is refused at upload, with a 422 whose errors carry one VARXR entry per missing archetype (AOM2 C_ARCHETYPE_ROOT validity rule VARXR); the 2013 CKM t_encounter_opt_test, built on the refused apgar, no longer loads, so the sandbox library pin is 231 accepted / 91 refused. A stored template whose constituent was deleted later answers its JSON form and example with the same VARXR list, and the viewer says so on every tab of the template, names each missing archetype and links to uploading it, instead of a raw 422 (#4505).

  • ADL 2 validation admits a constraint on an RM computed attribute. VCARM accepts an attribute “stored or computed” (AOM2 master04.5 §Validity Rules: C_ATTRIBUTE), and a function with no arguments is a computed attribute (master04.2 §Attribute Nodes), so an archetype that constrains DV_PROPORTION.is_integral, DV_QUANTITY.is_integral or EVENT.offset is no longer refused with 422. The generated RM model (openehr_rm::v1_2::model) now carries each class’s computed attributes from the BMM functions (RmClass::computed_attributes, computed_attribute). openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.microscopy_prostate_carcinoma.v1.0.0 from the 2013 CKM ADL 2 export now uploads, and the sandbox archetype-library pin moves to 232 accepted and 90 refused. DV_QUANTITY.property, which no RM release defines, stays refused. The nine openehr-* crates step to 0.0.124 (#4513).

  • DELETE /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/definition/artefact/adl2/{artefact_id} refuses with 409 Conflict while another stored ADL 2 artefact does not compile without the one deleted (a slot filler, a use_archetype reference or a specialisation parent, directly or through another artefact), and the message names every one of them. Before, the delete succeeded and left each template built on the archetype unable to compile (#4522).

  • The viewer’s ADL 2 template upload names each violation the CDR found when it refuses the source: every AOM2 rule code with the CDR’s words for it, so a template whose constituent archetype the CDR does not hold names that archetype (VARXR). The upload now asks for Prefer: return=representation, the preference under which ITS-REST lets a 4xx carry its error details, and reads the stored template’s id from the ETag of the 201 (#4523).

  • An ADL 2 operational template whose included archetype reuses the template’s node ids uploads again, where it was refused with 422 under VCOSU. Node-id uniqueness now holds per archetype and restarts at each C_ARCHETYPE_ROOT (AOM 2 VCOSU, “unique within the archetype”), and on an operational template the codes and interior node ids below a root are judged against that constituent’s entry in component_terminologies (OPT 2 master03-opt_raw). A duplicate node id inside one archetype is still refused. The nine openehr-* crates step to 0.0.125 (#4529).

  • The viewer’s dashboard draws the EHR or composition count as unavailable, with the reason in plain words, when the CDR answers its count query with a result set of another shape (no row, several rows, an empty row, several values, or a value that is no whole number), where it drew 0 before. The template Releases table draws such a count the same way. A real zero still draws 0 (#4533).

  • An ADL 2 operational template upload runs the terminology integrity rules (VTLC, VATCV, VTVSID, VTVSUQ, VTVSMD, VTTBK, VTCBK, and VTSD where the level is carried) on each component_terminologies entry, and each violation names the component’s archetype id (#4536).

  • A COMPOSITION committed against an ADL 2 operational template is validated against the template’s leaf constraints, where it was stored with 201 whatever it held. An inlined archetype recorded by its complete identifier (openEHR-EHR-OBSERVATION.x.v1.0.0, BASE master07-referencing §Reconstitutability) now matches its template node, so the C_INTEGER, C_REAL, C_STRING, C_BOOLEAN, tuple, value-set and cardinality constraints below it answer 422 (AOM 2 master04.5). An archetype root the template does not inline is refused as a node the template does not define, and a C_INTEGER or C_REAL list ({10, 15, 20}) admits each of its values where only the first was read. Canonical, FLAT and STRUCTURED commits take the same check. The nine openehr-* crates step to 0.0.127 (#4540).

  • A versioned read whose version path segment is no SEMVER version and no {major} or {major}.{minor} prefix, such as v1.x, 1.x or 01, now answers 400 before any lookup, where it answered 404 (parameters/path/version.yaml, responses/400.yaml). This covers the ADL 2 template read GET /definition/template/adl2/{template_id}/{version}, the stored-query read GET /definition/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version} and both stored-query executions at a version, GET and POST /query/{qualified_query_name}/{version}. A well-formed version the server does not hold still answers 404 (#4541).

  • A FLAT or STRUCTURED read of a COMPOSITION committed against an ADL 2 operational template returns the content below an inlined archetype that the composition records by its complete identifier (openEHR-EHR-OBSERVATION.x.v1.0.0, BASE master07-referencing §Reconstitutability). The read left out everything below such a root with no error; it now matches the root to its template node the way the commit does. The nine openehr-* crates step to 0.0.128 (#4551).

  • A COMPOSITION committed against an ADL 2 operational template whose C_INTEGER or C_REAL constraint is a union of ranges (for example magnitude matches {|0..5|, |10..15|}) is refused with 422 when the value lies outside every range. Such a value was stored. The served Web Template does not change: its input validation.range holds one range, so a union leaves it out, as before, and the check runs on the commit (#4552).

  • A FLAT or STRUCTURED read of a COMPOSITION committed against an ADL 2 operational template returns the value of an ELEMENT that holds a DV_INTERVAL whose lower and upper the template constrains. The read left the value out with no error (#4559).

  • A FLAT or STRUCTURED read of a COMPOSITION returns the value of an ELEMENT that holds a DV_INTERVAL whose template leaves the interval’s lower and upper unconstrained, for ADL 1.4 and ADL 2 templates. The read left the value out with no error, and a FLAT or STRUCTURED commit could not name the parts (#4559).

  • A COMPOSITION written from FLAT or STRUCTURED against an ADL 2 operational template carries what a canonical body built to that template carries. A node the template gives no term text, such as the HISTORY and ITEM_TREE of an OBSERVATION, is named for its RM type (History, Tree) instead of its bare id-code (id2). Every inlined archetype root records the complete identifier the template names (…cnf_minimal.v1.0.0, BASE master07-referencing §Reconstitutability) in its archetype_node_id and archetype_details.archetype_id, and archetype_details.rm_version is the template’s rm_release. Before this change the root recorded the interface form (…v1) and the server’s RM 1.2.0. Compositions built against an ADL 1.4 template keep their major-version archetype ids and RM 1.2.0 (#4560).

  • ferroehr report in a release build names the openehr-* crate versions that release published to crates.io: the release lanes stamp the published version into the checkout before they build the server, where the report used to name the floor the source tree holds. A new openehr_crates_origin field says published for a release build and source_tree for any other, a pre-release included (#4565).

  • An ADL 2 archetype reference resolves to one defined stored release: an interface reference (….v1) takes the newest release of its major version, a reference with a minor or patch version narrows the match to it, and an alpha or beta version matches only its full identifier (BASE Artefact Identification, Referencing). With several releases of one archetype stored, a template upload, an operational template and the delete’s dependents check used whichever release PostgreSQL returned last, and a reference to a major version no stored release carries resolved to another major version (#4567).

  • An ADL 2 upload and an ADL 2 delete no longer race. An upload validated before a concurrent delete of an archetype it uses committed could store a template whose constituent was gone. Both now hold one transaction-scoped advisory lock from the repository read to the commit, so the second write decides on what the first committed: an upload after the delete is refused with VARXR, and a delete after the upload is refused with a 409 naming the template (#4568).

  • The syslog form (DICOM PS3.15, IHE ITI-20) of an EHR-level audit record names its object beside the patient, as a URI participant object with the id its FHIR AuditEvent names. The record of placing, releasing or expiring an EHDS Art. 3(3) access delay names the held composition as access-delay:<vo>, so an Audit Record Repository fed by syslog can tell which composition a hold covers (#4569).

  • An ADL 2 template or archetype that references two major versions of one archetype (….v1 and ….v2), or one archetype under two namespaces, now compiles against both: the openehr-adl repository holds an artefact under its namespace, archetype and major version, and resolves each reference within that key (BASE Artefact Identification, Referencing). A reference without a namespace now resolves in the namespace of the artefact that makes it, and never in another namespace (#4579).

  • A read of a stored ADL 2 template by a partial id or a version (GET /definition/template/adl2/{template_id}) now resolves the way template compilation does: with v1.0.0 stored beside v1.0.0-rc.1, ….v1, ….v1.0 and version=1.0.0 answer the release in either upload order, and the release candidate is read only by its full version (BASE Artefact Identification, Referencing) (#4580).

  • A write that sends no committer, on a route that takes a bare RM body (the EHR_STATUS, COMPOSITION and DIRECTORY writes, and the demographic party and relationship writes), now records a Bearer caller’s login as issued by the token issuer, as EHR creation and every other default committer already did. It recorded the issuer ferroehr for every caller before; a Basic caller’s login is still issued by ferroehr (#4585).

  • The viewer’s ADL 1.4 template upload opens the stored template’s page, read from the ETag (else the Location) of the CDR’s 201, where it went to an address with no template id. A refused upload names each violation the CDR found, its rule code or path and the CDR’s words for it, as the ADL 2 upload does: the upload asks for Prefer: return=representation, the preference under which ITS-REST lets a 4xx carry its error details (#4596).

  • A 422 validation refusal tells the client to send Prefer: return=representation only when the request did not send it; a request that sent it receives the violations in errors and a detail without the advice (#4597).

  • An EHR Extract import refusal for a received version now names that version’s position in the extract (chapters[i]/items[j]/item/versions[k]), so an importer can find the defective ORIGINAL_VERSION in a large extract (#4602).

  • The import reads a version’s other_input_version_uids with the parser the CONTRIBUTION path uses and refuses an entry that is not an OBJECT_VERSION_ID, where it used to drop the entry. On the wire the extract decode already refuses such an entry with 422, so the import stays all or nothing (#4602).

  • An AQL archetype predicate matches the namespace exactly and reads the version it names as the oldest release it accepts within the major: org.a::… no longer finds data recorded in org.b, an id without a namespace finds only data recorded without one, and .v1.4.2 no longer finds data recorded under v1.0.0 (BASE Artefact Identification §Referencing and §Supporting Archetype-based Querying; #4629, #4630).

  • A query naming a parent archetype finds the data of a specialised child release only when that release declares a parent release at or after the queried one. Before, once one stored release of the child qualified, the data of every release of it was returned (BASE Artefact Identification, Referencing §Supporting Archetype-based Querying; #4637).

  • POST /definition/template/adl1.4 and POST /definition/template/adl2 answer 400 for every invalid template, the only refusal ITS-REST 1.1.0 declares for both uploads besides the 409 duplicate. An OPT that breaks the OPT 1.4 schema, an ADL 2 source that breaks an AOM2 rule such as VCORM or VCARM, and an ADL 2 template whose constituent archetype is not held were refused with 422. The problem keeps its detail and, with Prefer: return=representation, its errors. Upgrade note: a client that read a 422 from a template upload reads a 400, with the same detail and errors, under the about:blank problem type (#4643).

  • A directory create or update whose FOLDER carries an empty folders array, at the root or in a sub-folder, is refused with 400 and commits nothing. The ITS-JSON FOLDER schema gives folders minItems: 1, and the canonical JSON reader now refuses the empty array the same way in every document that carries a FOLDER, a CONTRIBUTION included. The viewer leaves folders out of a folder with no sub-folders (#4644).

  • A canonical XML FOLDER, EHR_STATUS, PERSON, AGENT, GROUP, ORGANISATION, ROLE or PARTY_RELATIONSHIP document now has the root element items with xsi:type naming its class, the element the ITS-XML schemas publish for a LOCATABLE (Structure.xsd). The directory reads (latest, by version and at a time), the EHR_STATUS reads, the demographic reads and the demographic template examples served <folder>, <ehr_status>, <person> and the like, which no ITS-XML schema declares. XML input accepts the same form (#4645).

  • POST /definition/template/adl1.4 builds the template’s Web Template before it stores the template, so a template it cannot build is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Once the template is stored, the upload answers 201 with its Location; with Prefer: return=representation and a Web Template Accept it serves the Web Template built before the store, and the OPT if that cannot be served. It no longer answers 422 for a template it has already stored (#4647).

  • A composition whose HISTORY carries events: [], and an AGENT, GROUP, ORGANISATION or PERSON carrying languages: [], are refused with 400 and commit nothing. The ITS-JSON schemas give both arrays minItems: 1, and the canonical JSON reader now refuses the empty array as it does an empty FOLDER folders. The FLAT builder no longer writes an empty events for a HISTORY that has no event (#4648).

  • A write to a restricted COMPOSITION (POST, PUT or DELETE on /ehr/{ehr_id}/composition) refused under a GDPR Art. 18 restriction now answers with the processing-restricted problem type, as the reads of a restricted record already did, in place of the generic forbidden type. The status stays 403 (#4657).

  • When an EXTRACT_SPEC criterion’s AQL runs past the query time budget, the 400 body now states the timeout as plain text. It used to start with a control-character marker that was only ever meant for the server itself (#4657).

  • Under a separated clinical credential, POST /ehr, PUT /ehr/{ehr_id} and an EHR_STATUS update that name a subject no longer fail with a database error: the subject pseudonym guard reads the deployment posture, and the clinical role now holds SELECT on ext.posture through the ext migration 0009 (#4675).

  • A cohort that names its subjects now finds, under [ehr_index] provider = "local", the EHR created over POST /ehr with that subject in its EHR_STATUS; it read a cross-reference table no route wrote, so it matched nothing. A cohort predicate and the AQL demographic join resolve a party to the EHRs whose EHR_STATUS.subject names it. The EHR_STATUS subject is now the one source of which EHR belongs to which subject. Upgrade note: linkage.subject_ehr and the linkage.erase_ehr function go with the linkage schema, which audit migration 0021 drops with the linkage domain. Rows written there through the service API are dropped with the table; the EHRs they named keep their subject in their own EHR_STATUS (#4675).

  • The identifier scan ([privacy.identifier_scan]) no longer refuses a DV_IDENTIFIER whose type declares an item rather than a person, such as a laboratory filler_order_number that passes the NHS Number check by chance. A DV_IDENTIFIER in FEEDER_AUDIT.originating_system_item_ids or feeder_system_item_ids is scanned only when its type names a person identifier. A type naming a person (patient, NHS, BSN, social security and similar) keeps the value scanned in every slot, and free text and untyped identifiers in clinical content are scanned as before. The default rule set is unchanged; a deployment that knows its jurisdictions still narrows rules, so a Dutch one with rules = ["nl-bsn"] never claims an NHS Number (#4702).

  • An inline primitive constraint in a parsed archetype or template now carries the node id AOM2 ADL_CODE_DEFINITIONS.Primitive_node_id defines, at9999 in an at-coded archetype and id9999 in an id-coded one, where it carried the constant’s name Primitive_node_id. An ADL 1.4 archetype converted to ADL2 gets the id-coded form (#4739).

  • The ABAC policy-enforcement point checks every item-tag operation as it checks its target: a COMPOSITION tag read after the call like the COMPOSITION read, a COMPOSITION tag write before the call with the tagged version’s template, category and origin, and the EHR tag read before the call like the EHR read. These operations were unchecked before, so a patient-scoped or template-scoped rule now refuses a tag read or write wherever it refuses the target’s read or write. A COMPOSITION tag read also falls under the EHR_ACCESS privacy ceiling and its audit record names the tagged COMPOSITION (#4768).

  • Under spec_profile = "stable", a canonical-JSON party read lists in reverse_relationships every PARTY_RELATIONSHIP another party’s current version carries with this party as its target, one LOCATABLE_REF each naming the source party’s version container and the relationship’s path, as RM 1.1.0 §Party Relationships requires. The development profile, whose RM 1.2.0 makes the attribute a function, is unchanged. The released-profile conformance run now judges the server on the stable profile (#4775).

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: both fixes exist only in ferrohealth-server releases that carry functional changes in the same serving path beside them (0.3.7 two fixes, 0.3.8 and 0.3.9 the problem details module, the kept listener TLS and the unmasked remedy), so there is no security-only release of the crate for FerroEHR to take, and the client CA refusal ships in the release candidate the advisory names.

  • FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.7 in place of 0.3.5 (GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg). Every earlier release held a plain-HTTP connection that never sent a byte for as long as the client kept it open, so about 8400 silent connections from a client with no credentials exhausted the quickstart’s file descriptors and the CDR stopped answering, health checks included; the listener then retried a failed accept at once and logged every failure. Such a connection now closes once [server] header_read_timeout_ms passes (30 s by default), counted from accept, and after an EMFILE or ENFILE the listener pauses up to 1 s before it accepts again and logs one warning every 10 seconds (#4283).

  • A [server.tls] table that sets client_ca_file with client_auth at none, written or by default, is refused at load, naming the setting (GHSA-52mf-qg39-4q4j). Before 5.5.0 a client CA alone meant that every client presents a certificate; 5.5.0 moved the listener onto ferrohealth-server, where client_auth defaults to none and the CA was read and ignored, so a configuration carried over passed config check and served without asking a client certificate. FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.9, which refuses it and names the remedy in full. A 5.5.0 deployer who sets client_ca_file sets client_auth = "required" beside it. The default template no longer pairs a client CA with none, and says what each client_auth value does (#4349).

  • CVE-2026-84243, the glibc gettext LANGUAGE directory traversal (GLIBC-SA-2026-0025), has no Debian fix for trixie yet and is judged not_affected in every image. The ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer programs never leave the C locale, so glibc ignores LANGUAGE and opens no message catalog (security/vex/ferroehr-os.openvex.json). In ferroehr-postgres only the container environment the operator writes can set LANGUAGE; no database connection can (security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json) (#4500).

5.6.0-rc7 - 2026-11-01

5.6.0-rc7 is the seventh release candidate of 5.6.0, published for testing. It carries the CONTRIBUTION break of 5.6.0-rc6: POST /ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution and POST /demographic/contribution read the body through the released NewContribution schema and answer 400 for a lifecycle_state that is no DV_CODED_TEXT, a description that is a plain string or an object without _type, an audit without change_type, an audit typed ATTESTATION or UPDATE_ATTESTATION, a missing audit or versions, and a preceding_version_uid sent as a plain string, and a stated empty system_id is refused with 422 on every write path (#3595, #4543). These notes carry every change since 5.5.0, those of the 5.6.0-rc6, 5.6.0-rc5, 5.6.0-rc4 and 5.6.0-rc3 sections below included. New since 5.6.0-rc6: the EHDS Art. 10 opt-out from access through the access services, off by default until [authz.rbac] access_service_roles declares the access-service roles, with the Art. 10(2) vital-interest override marked as an emergency (#4516); every write’s committer checked against the authenticated caller (#4520) and a Bearer caller’s default committer issued by the token issuer (#4585); ADL 2 FLAT and STRUCTURED writes that carry the names, archetype references and RM release the template gives (#4560), a served Web Template that writes a bound coded input as the bound terms (#4574) and gives every DV_INTERVAL its lower and upper parts (#4559); ADL 2 validation that checks a C_INTEGER or C_REAL union of ranges (#4552), a repository keyed by namespace, archetype and major version (#4579), a read that resolves a release before its pre-releases (#4580) and an upload and a delete ordered by one lock (#4568); an AQL archetype predicate that matches the namespace exactly and the version as the oldest release (#4629, #4630); a CONTRIBUTION that records its merge inputs and accepts the UPDATE_VERSION members the schema leaves open (#4577), and an EHR Extract import that refuses a malformed merge input and names the version’s position (#4602); the syslog form of an access-delay record naming the held composition (#4569); the viewer’s ADL 2 and ADL 1.4 uploads naming each violation the CDR found (#4523, #4596); storage generation 4 and its benchmark records (#4525); ferroehr report naming the published openehr-* crate versions in a release build (#4565); and response texts without the Service Model vocabulary (#4531, #4634). The conformance run on main under the released profile fails no row against the server and still has one errored row, Veredictum’s own (Vernum-Projecten/Veredictum#964, closed upstream after the pinned 0.3.2, which still errors on it), and the triage on #4455 stays open, so this candidate does not claim a green Veredictum record. 5.5.0 stays the stable release: this pre-release moves neither the latest image tags, the book under /docs/latest/ nor the hosted sandbox, it publishes no crates, and it receives no fixes; the next release candidate or 5.6.0 itself replaces it. Before you try it: a write whose committer names another login of the caller’s token issuer or of this server, or a PARTY_SELF committer from a caller who is not the record’s person, answers 403, and a direct write whose committer breaks its own rules answers 422; a write that sends no committer on a bare RM body route records a Bearer caller’s login as issued by the token issuer, where it recorded ferroehr; an AQL archetype predicate matches the namespace exactly and reads the version it names as the oldest release it accepts, so a query may find less than before; a FLAT or STRUCTURED composition under an ADL 2 template records the complete archetype identifier and the template’s rm_release, and the served Web Template writes a bound coded input, COMPOSITION.category among them, as the bound terms (openehr::433) where it wrote the local at-code; a CONTRIBUTION commit must take the shapes above; a write under a token whose SMART resource scopes are all patient/ scopes records PARTY_SELF as committer and may change only what the person committed, and a service auth_failure answers 403 where it answered 500; a versioned read whose version is no SEMVER version or prefix answers 400 where it answered 404; the served Web Template of an ADL 2 template writes a data value’s aqlPath without an [idN] predicate; a composition that breaks an ADL 2 template’s leaf constraint, and an ADL 2 template whose constituent archetype is not held, answer 422; every route ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define moves from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/ to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/, and the ITI-81 retrieval to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent, with no redirect from the old paths; an error body is application/problem+json, so a client that read message reads detail, and one that read validationErrors sends Prefer: return=representation and reads errors; audit migration 0017 refuses an audit store that holds records written by 5.5.0 or earlier, while an audit store that 5.6.0-rc2 migrated upgrades in place; a [server.tls] table with client_ca_file must set client_auth = "required" (or "optional") beside it, or the configuration is refused at load; [server] header_read_timeout_ms no longer bounds an idle kept-alive connection, which the new [server] idle_timeout_ms (120000 by default) closes, so keep it longer than the idle timeout of your clients and load balancers; a client that wrote a space as + in a query string sends %20; a party delete names the latest OBJECT_VERSION_ID in its path and answers 400 for a versioned object id; a body the RM refuses after the ITS-JSON schema admits it answers 422, and a misplaced CONTRIBUTION member, a Simplified Format commit without openehr-template-id and a flat |raw value without _type answer 400; a tag update under Prefer: return=identifier answers 200 with the tag list; with [authz.rbac] enabled a token holding only system/ SMART on openEHR scopes reaches clinical operations without a role; the viewer image serves no /pkg/ and reads no LEPTOS_SITE_ROOT, LEPTOS_OUTPUT_NAME or LEPTOS_HASH_FILES, and its Content-Security-Policy is script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; Helm chart 21.0.0-rc7 refuses to render until config.deployment_profile names sandbox or production, and a values file for its FerroPIX moves ferropix.config.server.public_base_url to ferropix.config.public_base_url and each issuer’s clients to ferropix.config.trust.issuer. Storage generation 3 adds node columns and migrates no data, and ext migration 0008 names generation 4, the generation with the node header columns, and changes only the label; clinical migration 0020 adds the origin to retention policies and 0021 statistics on the archetype columns, and clinical 0022 and 0023 and party 0013 and 0014 rebuild the version tree’s uniqueness constraint and index its version id columns, which reads every version row of an existing store once; clinical 0024 and party 0015 index the version uid, ext 0006, clinical 0025 and party 0016 add the ELEMENT value search index, built over every hot node row of an existing store, party 0017 adds the archetype statistics, and clinical 0026 and party 0018 grant MAINTAIN on the partitioned tables to the serving roles; clinical 0027 and party 0019 add the access delay, and ext 0007, clinical 0028 and party 0020 add the node header columns with no data migrated; audit migration 0019 gives the search token index a pending list of 512 kB, and audit 0020 adds the hash index on request_id; clinical 0029 adds the access opt-out. Helm chart 21.0.0-rc7 carries appVersion 5.6.0-rc7. Security carries two advisories, GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg and GHSA-52mf-qg39-4q4j, and the OpenVEX judgement of CVE-2026-84243.

Added

  • The logging component’s intended performance is stated as checkable claims (EHDS Annex II 1.1): every composition create and read recorded exactly once and every AQL execution at least once, no access succeeding without its record, at most 125 % of the latency and at least 80 % of the throughput with the access log off, and a 50-record ITI-81 page within 250 ms at p95. scripts/perf/audit.sh measures them with the access log off and on (the load test’s new --audit mode counts the records through ITI-81 and times retrievals), scripts/perf/audit-verdict.sh gives the verdict, the release refuses a claim not met and attaches the summary as ferroehr-<tag>-logging-performance.md (Annex III point 2), and the weekly performance guard runs it on main. The book’s compliance section gains the page that states the claims and the method (#4293).

  • scripts/interop/atna.sh exercises the logging component’s ATNA transactions against independent implementations run from published images (EHDS Annex II 1.4): the ITI-20 FHIR feed into HAPI FHIR as the Audit Record Repository, judged by its validator with IHE BALP 1.1.4; the ITI-20 syslog feed into syslog-ng over RFC 5425 TLS, each payload read as a DICOM PS3.15 AuditMessage; and the same ITI-81 searches put to FerroEHR and to HAPI. The audit trail page documents it (#4296).

  • FerroEHR ships an EHDS category map for the published CKM templates and COMPOSITION archetypes whose data sit in one Art. 14(1) priority category (the International Patient Summary, ePrescription, the generic laboratory result and CCTA report templates; the health_summary, prescription and transfer_summary archetypes), so an installation that declares no [audit.categories] keys records those accesses classified instead of unclassified (EHDS Annex II 3.2(c)). A deployment that declares any template or archetype replaces it whole. [audit.categories] shipped_map = false with nothing declared leaves no map, which deployment_profile = "production" refuses as the new no_category_map gap unless deployment_accepts names it (#4298).

  • Retention periods and access rules can take the origin and the category of the data into account (EHDS Annex II 3.4). The new top-level [origins] register declares the origins a deployment recognises, each by the id its data carry and the clients whose direct commits come from it; a body without a FEEDER_AUDIT committed by a registered client is stamped with that client’s origin instead of the server’s system_id. PUT /admin/retention/policy takes an optional origin naming a registered origin, the register and GET /admin/retention/due report it, and the due list lists an origin-keyed period over the objects of that origin (clinical migration 0020_retention_by_origin.sql). The ABAC request carries category (the access record’s category tokens) and origin resource attributes on composition, contribution and query operations, the Cedar schema declares both, and a remote PDP binding may name them as parameters (#4299).

  • The operations page gains a storage sizing section, measured on 5.6.0-rc5: about 21.6 KB of clinical storage per version of a vital signs composition (2.0 times its canonical JSON, 85 % of it node rows) and 155 KB for an International Patient Summary, about 1.2 KB per audit record of a read, the effect of [audit.store] retention on growth, pg_wal up to max_wal_size, the REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY clinical.node_hot_pkey step (20 % of that index after heavy concurrent writing) and a query for the size per relation, with the method to reproduce the figures (#4304).

  • EHDS Art. 5: what a person inserts in their own EHR is marked as theirs, and they cannot alter what a professional committed. A write under a token whose SMART resource scopes are all patient/ scopes records PARTY_SELF as its AUDIT_DETAILS.committer, its external_ref naming the login, whatever committer the request names; a COMPOSITION it commits must name PARTY_SELF or PARTY_RELATED as composer; and its update or deletion of a version whose committer is not PARTY_SELF, directly or inside a CONTRIBUTION, is refused with 403. A professional’s writes are unchanged. The contribution list extension gains inserted_by_person per row, and the viewer names a PARTY_SELF committer “The person or their representative”. A service auth_failure status now answers 403 where it answered 500 (#4350).

  • The EHDS Art. 3(3) delay of the person’s own access to newly registered data, a Member State option and off by default. The new [access_delay] section (enabled, categories, hours) holds every new COMPOSITION of a listed [audit.categories] category from requests that may be the person’s own (a bearer token with a SMART patient/ grant or the ABAC patient claim, also beside user/ or system/ grants, as ferrohealth-smart 0.8.7 decides it) for at most hours: a read answers 404 as for an unknown composition, and a query, an export and a CONTRIBUTION leave it out, while a professional reads it as before. The treating professional releases a held composition from the clinical route POST {ext}/ehr/{ehr_id}/versioned_composition/{versioned_object_uid}/access-delay/release, with the checks of a write to that EHR, and the controller with POST /admin/access-delay/release; a professional holds one by hand within the limit with POST /admin/access-delay and reads the register with GET /admin/access-delay; every hold ends at its limit, and placing, releasing and expiry are each an access record. The subject-scoped ITI-81 read of the person’s own trail (EHDS Art. 9) leaves out the records about a held composition until it is released or expires, then serves them with their original times (ehds-logging 0.3.3) (clinical migration 0027_access_delay.sql, party migration 0019_access_delay_column.sql) (#4351).

  • The openehr-its client reads an RFC 9457 problem details refusal: ErrorBody::problem() exposes its type, title, status, detail and instance, ignoring a member of the wrong type (RFC 9457 §3.1), and ErrorBody::message() answers the problem’s detail, else its title, where it answered only the ITS-REST Error’s message. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.115 (#4355).

  • The local EHR index ([ehr_index] provider = "local") is a supported production posture beside the IHE patient identity source: EHR_STATUS.subject names a patient by its own namespace and identifier, which GET /ehr?subject_id=&subject_namespace= matches, and with no [privacy] subject_namespaces declared the reference is stored as the client sends it. The compose quickstart selects it with FERROEHR_EHR_INDEX=local docker compose up, which runs its ferroehr-config-local block (#4379).

  • CI checks every inline configuration of the compose quickstart with the config check of the image the file pins, FerroEHR’s and FerroPIX’s, so the quickstart can no longer carry a configuration its pinned server refuses (#4380).

  • The Conformance workflow runs the Veredictum 0.3.0 catalogue in CI through the Veredictum GitHub Action, pinned by commit SHA and running the release image by digest. It builds FerroEHR from the commit, composes it with FerroTERM beside it on fresh volumes, reviews the party statement with veredictum validate, fails on a failed or errored row, writes the Markdown summary to the job summary and uploads the results, JUnit and CTRF views. It runs on pull requests that touch the server, the party set, the conformance compose files or the workflow, on main, on a release tag and twice a week. scripts/conformance.sh takes a stage (run, review, up, down), so CI and a local run compose the same deployment, and scripts/checks/veredictum-action.sh fails while the Action SHA, its version comment, the image digest and VEREDICTUM_VERSION disagree (#4449).

  • The Conformance workflow runs the Veredictum smart documents (smart_discovery, smart_scopes) against the same FerroEHR build after the Veredictum Action, which forwards no SMART Platform base URL and no scoped tokens. The same pinned image runs veredictum test with --platform-url and docs/conformance/party/ferroehr/ixit-smart.json, minting each access token in memory from the committed test issuer the SMART overlay trusts, and the job uploads its results, JUnit and CTRF views beside the catalogue’s and adds its summary under a heading of its own. scripts/conformance.sh gains the smart stage, and run drives it after the catalogue, so a local run covers SMART too (#4450).

  • GET /ehr/{ehr_id} and GET /ehr?subject_id=… now send Last-Modified: the commit that created the EHR, or the later commit that added or deleted one of its folder hierarchies (#4462).

  • The EHDS Art. 10 opt-out from access through the access services of Arts. 4 and 12, a Member State option and off by default. The new [authz.rbac] access_service_roles key declares the roles of the access-service callers; while an EHR carries the opt-out, a caller holding one reads it as absent: a route naming the EHR or an object in it answers 404 as for an unknown EHR, a population query leaves its data out, a scoped query, an export and the lookup by subject find no such EHR, and a write to it is refused as absent. Every other caller, the provider’s own care included, reads it as before. The controller records the opt-out on the person’s instruction with POST /admin/access-opt-out, reverses it with POST /admin/access-opt-out/reverse (the register keeps the reversal) and reads the register with GET /admin/access-opt-out; recording is refused with 400 while no access-service role is declared. An access-service caller that declares one of [audit] emergency_purpose_codes and does not act for the person reads the EHR under the Art. 10(2) vital-interest override, with the emergency mark on its access record and an access-opt-out-override record against the EHR. Recording, reversing and reading the register are access records (clinical migration 0029_access_opt_out.sql) (#4516).

Changed

  • Breaking for clients that relied on the old leniencies: POST /ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution and POST /demographic/contribution now read the body through the released NewContribution schema, and refuse every shape it does not define. Each refused shape answers 400: (#3595)

    • a lifecycle_state in the CODE_PHRASE shape {"terminology_id": …, "code_string": …}, as a plain string, or as a bare {"value": …}. Send a DV_CODED_TEXT: {"value": "complete", "defining_code": {"terminology_id": {"value": "openehr"}, "code_string": "532"}};
    • a description sent as a plain string, on the contribution audit, on a commit_audit or on an attestation. Send a DV_TEXT or DV_CODED_TEXT object: {"_type": "DV_TEXT", "value": "…"};
    • a commit_audit or contribution audit without change_type. The server no longer infers creation or modification from preceding_version_uid; send the code of the change, for example 249 (creation), 251 (modification), 523 (deleted) or 666 (attestation);
    • a commit_audit or contribution audit whose _type is ATTESTATION or UPDATE_ATTESTATION, or any value other than UPDATE_AUDIT or AUDIT_DETAILS. Send the audit as UPDATE_AUDIT (or with no _type) and put each attestation in the version’s attestations list as an UPDATE_ATTESTATION. A 666 (attestation) version carries its attestations there too, and one with no attestation is refused;
    • a missing audit, which answered 422 before. A missing versions list, an attestation without reason or is_pending, a system_id that is not a string, and a preceding_version_uid sent as a plain string instead of {"value": "…"} are refused the same way.

  • An attestation’s own system_id is kept, and one that states none takes the system_id of the version audit it belongs to instead of the server’s. An attestation committer is now checked against its PARTY_PROXY rules like every other committer, so an invalid one answers 422 (#3595).

  • The served OpenAPI document describes each extension route by what it does and by the ITS-REST text that governs it, and no longer names openEHR Service Model operations, interfaces or status codes. Routes, request and response fields and status codes are unchanged (#4213).

  • A population AQL query that only counts its root objects, such as SELECT COUNT(c) FROM EHR e CONTAINS COMPOSITION c or the same with COUNT(*), reads the current version rows and no longer probes the root node of every composition. At 545 000 compositions the count fell from about 9 s to 0.2 s (#4286).

  • A REST request checks a connection out of each database pool once and keeps it until it answers, where it took one for each statement: two to four checkouts for a read of an EHR, an EHR_STATUS or a COMPOSITION, each waiting in the pool’s queue under load and each paying the pool’s release round trip. At 48 concurrent clients and a pool of 10, throughput rose by about 18 % and the median latency fell by about 13 % (#4289).

  • The Helm chart, at a new major version (21), has no default deployment profile: it refuses to render until config.deployment_profile names sandbox or production, so an installation that follows a quickstart instead of the instructions for use no longer runs the sandbox posture by omission (EHDS Annex II 1.2). A values file that relied on the old sandbox default must now set it, for example --set config.deployment_profile=sandbox; values-production.yaml sets production as before. The server binary’s own default and the Compose files, which declare sandbox explicitly, are unchanged (#4294).

  • The audit store keeps each record’s facts in columns and renders its FHIR R4 AuditEvent from them when the record is read over ITI-81 or delivered by the FHIR feed, instead of storing the rendered document in every record. A record takes about a quarter of the space it took before. The configuration the rendering depends on (the audit source, the store horizon, the category map and the emergency purposes) is kept once per distinct configuration in audit.audit_render_policy, and every record names the policy it was written under, so it renders the same document after the configuration changes. The tamper chain hashes every column of the record in one digest and checks each render policy against its digest; the earlier digest versions are retired. Audit migration 0017 needs an empty audit store and refuses one that holds records written by an earlier release, naming the remedy. ITI-81 parameters on an element of the document (address, the .identifier parameters, entity-type, entity-role, type, subtype) are matched against the rendered document (#4300).

  • The three audit indexes on recorded_at ascend, so their pages fill instead of splitting half full on every insert; the newest-first ITI-81 search scans them backward (#4302).

  • A clinical or party node row now stores only the part of its canonical JSON fragment that its own columns do not hold: _type, a lowercase archetype_node_id, a plain or simply coded name, and an ELEMENT value in one of the common basic shapes (a quantity, count, ordinal, coded or plain text, date, time, duration, identifier, boolean or URI) move into columns, the value into the new typed value columns. Every reader rebuilds the omitted keys, so the canonical JSON and every AQL result are unchanged, and a filter on a quantity’s magnitude or a code reads its column directly. The node heap shrinks by about a third (storage generation 3); a row written before keeps its whole fragment and reads the same. Migrations ext/0005, clinical/0019 and party/0012 add the columns and the readers; no data is migrated (#4306).

  • Every ITI-81 search parameter answers through an index again. The store takes the search tokens of a record’s rendered AuditEvent when it writes the record: each distinct token once in audit.audit_search_token, the code-system tokens (type, subtype, entity-type, entity-role, source.identifier) as one shared set in audit.audit_search_set, and their ids on the record in search_tokens under a GIN index; entity reads a hash index on resource_id. A search on address or a token parameter no longer renders every record in its date window. The tamper chain covers search_tokens, and the verifier reports a changed token or set (#4313).

  • The storage-bench lane measures the baseline and the candidate on one runner in eight interleaved rounds each and gives two verdicts. The plan verdict fails an operation whose median pages per call rose more than 10 % and one page above the baseline’s highest round, whatever its time. The time verdict divides each round by its machine factor, so a slow spell of the runner no longer reads as the code, and fails an operation whose median p50 or p99 rose more than 15 % with every candidate round slower than every baseline round, or a candidate build that ran more than 15 % slower across the board in every round. A latency is no longer compared with a record measured on another runner (#4318).

  • The viewer takes FerroUI 0.5.8: a menu item draws a visible bar under the pointer and the keyboard focus, and the top bar’s search no longer opens its panel again over the page the router draws after a search is submitted or one of its options followed (#4319).

  • Nothing ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define is served under the openEHR base path any more. FerroEHR serves three namespaces beside each other under /ferroehr/rest/: /openehr/v1/ holds only the ITS-REST routes, /fhir/r4/ the FHIR and IHE interfaces, and /extensions/v1/ FerroEHR’s own extensions. The ITI-81 retrieval moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/fhir/r4/AuditEvent to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent. These routes moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/... to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/... with the same relative path: /terminology/..., /admin/event_subscription..., /demographic/party_relationship..., /demographic/versioned_party_relationship/..., /definition/archetype/..., /definition/artefact/..., /message/export..., /message/import..., /query/cohort, and the admin extensions /admin/config, /admin/template/{template_id}, /admin/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version}, /admin/party/..., /admin/archive/..., /admin/report/..., /admin/dump, /admin/load, /admin/integrity/..., /admin/restriction..., /admin/access-restriction..., /admin/research-objection and /admin/retention/.... The old paths answer 404, with no redirect. The served OpenAPI document and its family documents name the new paths; the admin extensions, the archetype library and the cohort query have family documents of their own (admin-extensions, archetypes, cohort, contributions). The paged CONTRIBUTION list moved too, to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution (#4330).

  • The server and viewer images build on the current gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot digest, so they carry the base image’s latest Debian package updates (#4335).

  • Canonical JSON validation against the openEHR ITS-JSON schemas runs on jsonschema 0.59.0, which refuses a value whose regex match the engine cannot finish where 0.58 accepted it under not or patternProperties. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.113 (#4336).

  • A statement the database cancels, by its statement_timeout or a cancel request (SQLSTATE 57014), answers 503 with Retry-After instead of 500: the statement rolled back, so the request can be repeated.
