These routes moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/... to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/... with the same relative path: /terminology/..., /admin/event_subscription..., /demographic/party_relationship..., /demographic/versioned_party_relationship/..., /definition/archetype/..., /definition/artefact/..., /message/export..., /message/import..., /query/cohort, and the admin extensions /admin/config, /admin/template/{template_id}, /admin/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version}, /admin/party/..., /admin/archive/..., /admin/report/..., /admin/dump, /admin/load, /admin/integrity/..., /admin/restriction..., /admin/access-restriction..., /admin/research-objection and /admin/retention/.... The old paths answer 404, with no redirect. The served OpenAPI document and its family documents name the new paths; the admin extensions, the archetype library and the cohort query have family documents of their own (admin-extensions, archetypes, cohort, contributions). The paged CONTRIBUTION list moved too, to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution (#4330).

  • The server and viewer images build on the current gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot digest, so they carry the base image’s latest Debian package updates (#4335).

  • Canonical JSON validation against the openEHR ITS-JSON schemas runs on jsonschema 0.59.0, which refuses a value whose regex match the engine cannot finish where 0.58 accepted it under not or patternProperties. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.113 (#4336).

  • A statement the database cancels, by its statement_timeout or a cancel request (SQLSTATE 57014), answers 503 with Retry-After instead of 500: the statement rolled back, so the request can be repeated. By default the request timeout answers before the 60 s statement timeout fires, so on a request path it is raised by an operator’s cancel or by a forward step of the database host’s clock, which fires every running statement’s timeout at once (#4338).

  • Every error on the openEHR routes (/ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/), the extension routes (/ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/) and the management routes answers RFC 9457 problem details, application/problem+json, in place of the { message, validationErrors, error } body shaped after the ITS-REST example. The status codes are unchanged. A problem carries type, title, status, detail and the request id as a urn:uuid: instance; the refusals a client acts on have FerroEHR types documented on the book’s Problem types page (aql-invalid, query-timeout, validation-failed, content-invalid, conflict, version-conflict, unauthenticated, forbidden, processing-restricted, unavailable, rate-limited), every other error is about:blank. A request with Prefer: return=representation receives the additional details ITS-REST allows: the violations of a validation refusal as errors ({path, detail}, where validationErrors held "<path>: <message>" strings), the byte position of an AQL parse refusal, and the current_version of a 412. The stack’s own 408, 413, 429, 503 and panic 500 are problems too, and an OperationOutcome under the FHIR base, where an authentication refusal is now an OperationOutcome as well. The served OpenAPI document declares the Problem schema for every 4xx and 5xx, and the viewer reads problem details. A client that read message reads detail; one that read validationErrors sends Prefer: return=representation and reads errors (#4342).

  • The FHIR AuditEvent of an EHDS access record names the object it reads, creates, updates or deletes by its openEHR object id as entity.what.identifier with the system urn:openehr:object-id, where it wrote a what.reference that no FHIR server resolves and HAPI FHIR refused (FHIR R4 references.html §2.3.0.3). ITI-81 finds the record by entity.identifier. FerroEHR takes FerroAUDIT 0.3.2 (ihe-atna and ehds-logging) (#4366).

  • The access log costs the request path less under load. The audit store writes a drained batch, its search tokens and its token sets in one transaction on one connection (one commit where it took up to three), stores only the tokens it does not hold yet, and the GIN index on search_tokens takes new entries through a pending list of 512 kB. On the release load test the store wrote 1.5 KB of WAL per record where it wrote 5.2 KB (#4375).

  • [ehr_index] provider = "local" beside pixm_url, assigning_authority, [ehr_index.oauth] or [ehr_index.tls] is accepted, where it was refused: the IHE keys are kept, not used and named at boot, so provider alone switches the index, in the file or as FERROEHR__EHR_INDEX__PROVIDER. Declared pseudonym namespaces stay in force under either index (#4379).

  • A build no release lane marked reports its commit beside the package version, as SemVer build metadata (5.6.0-rc2+dev.1a2b3c4d5e6f), on ferroehr --version and server_version of GET /ferroehr/rest/status (the boot banner and /management/info already name the commit beside the version), so a report from a build of main no longer reads as the release it follows; a release build reports the bare version (#4380).

  • The compose quickstart runs FerroPIX 0.0.12, pinned by digest, with its configuration moved to that release’s keys (public_base_url at the top level, the Patient Identity Source’s client under [[trust.issuer]]), and Dependabot proposes each FerroPIX release (#4380).

  • The Helm chart runs FerroPIX 0.0.12 by digest, with the FerroPIX chart 0.3.4 built for it, and the hosted sandbox runs FerroPIX 0.0.12 too; both had stayed at 0.0.7 and 0.0.10 when the quickstart moved. A values file for the chart’s FerroPIX moves ferropix.config.server.public_base_url to ferropix.config.public_base_url and each issuer’s clients to ferropix.config.trust.issuer, the keys FerroPIX reads since 0.0.8; the chart’s examples and the production overlay do. FerroPIX’s chart now also runs its pods with enableServiceLinks: false and in a user namespace (ferropix.hostUsers: false, the default). A CI guard holds the quickstart, chart and sandbox to one FerroPIX release and checks the sandbox’s and the chart’s FerroPIX configuration under it, so the Dependabot proposal for the quickstart pin moves all three (#4392).

  • openehr-query, the AQL 1.1.0 lexer, parser, typed AST and printer, is published under Apache-2.0 from 0.0.116, like the generated model crates and openehr-its, so any Rust project can parse AQL with it. Versions 0.0.60 to 0.0.115 keep the Business Source License 1.1 they were published under (#4405).

  • FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.4.0 in place of 0.3.9. The new [server] idle_timeout_ms (120000 by default) closes a kept-alive HTTP/1.1 connection that waits that long for its next request, with a clean end of stream, and [server] header_read_timeout_ms counts from the first byte of each request head on a kept-alive connection (from accept for the first one, as before). The head bound used to count from the end of the previous answer, so it also closed an idle connection after 30 s, sometimes as a client sent its next request into it, which a client such as Go’s net/http saw as EOF on a POST it does not retry (#4381). A deployment that set header_read_timeout_ms to bound idle connections sets idle_timeout_ms instead. The refusals the listener writes itself (408, 413, 429, 503) and a panic’s 500 keep naming the server’s request id as their instance when the client sends its own X-Request-Id, as every other FerroEHR refusal does (#4417).

Fixed

  • The hosted sandbox seeds its full demo dataset again. The v5.5.0 reseed stopped at the ADL 2 archetype library (233 stored / 89 refused against the pinned 231 / 91) because the box’s .env still forced FerroTERM 0.1.6, which reads none of the FerroTERM 0.3 settings the sandbox posture passes, so it served no LOINC and VETDF could only warn on braden_scale’s mistyped LA9605-4. The corpus, the pin and the CDR were right. The seed now asks the CDR for a LOINC code before the library step and names a posture without LOINC (SANDBOX_TERMINOLOGY=without-loinc opts a local run into 233 / 89), checks that the two files it names move together, and a corpus test holds the manifest’s pin to the adjudicated split with and without LOINC. The FerroPIX rollout script retires a stale FERROTERM_IMAGE override, checks that FerroTERM runs the pinned version and serves LOINC, and wipes before it seeds over an unfinished seed (#4278).

  • The measurement overlay docker/sut-measurement.yml switches the caller rate limiter off by removing the [server.caller_rate] keys, so the server logs caller rate limiting configured with enabled=false at boot, instead of setting a rate of 4294967295 per second that ferrohealth-server 0.3.5 truncated to a zero interval and that answered stray 429s under concurrency. scripts/conformance.sh refuses to start a measurement stack whose ferroehr service still sets a caller rate (#4281).

  • A response to a request whose body FerroEHR left unread, such as a 404 to a POST of a path it does not serve or a declared-length 413, now carries Connection: close. The connection closed after such a response without saying so, and a client that sent its next request on it met a closed socket, which a non-idempotent request cannot safely retry (RFC 9112 §9.6) (#4283).

  • A [server.caller_rate] above 1 000 000 000 requests per second no longer answers 429 to concurrent requests: such a rate now limits nothing, as its operator meant (#4283).

  • Every request leaves one request line, a timeout 408, a declared-length 413 and the 500 of a panicked handler included, and a 413 for a body with no declared length that passes [server] body_limit_bytes is answered with the openEHR error body, as the declared-length 413 is (#4283).

  • An AQL query whose WHERE clause chains thousands of NOT, AND or OR terms no longer overflows the stack and aborts the server. The parser refuses a query that nests brackets and CONTAINS deeper than 64 levels or builds an expression deeper than 512 levels with 400 Bad Request, before any recursive pass runs, on the ad-hoc, stored-query store and execution paths alike. A long OR over one path is written as MATCHES {…}, which the bound does not count. A statement PostgreSQL refuses for its own complexity limit (SQLSTATE class 54) also answers 400 instead of 500. openehr-query gains ParseError::TooDeep (#4284).

  • An AQL query (ad hoc or stored) whose client disconnects, or that the server’s own query.timeout_ms or HTTP request timeout gives up on, no longer keeps its statement running and its pooled connection busy until the statement ends. The connection is closed instead of returned to the pool, so the slot frees at once, and every pooled session now sets PostgreSQL’s client_connection_check_interval to one second, so the backend stops the abandoned statement within about a second. The composition-count statistics behave the same way (#4285).

  • The server’s resident memory no longer climbs under sustained load until the container’s memory limit kills it. The ferroehr binary now allocates through mimalloc instead of glibc malloc, whose per-thread arenas kept freed memory and never gave it back. On a load test of 10 000 mixed jobs at 48 workers the peak resident set fell from 2.3 to 3.2 GB (growing run after run) to about 600 MB, and throughput rose by about a third (#4288).

  • A request whose database connection a PostgreSQL restart, a crash or the network cuts now answers 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After, as a request that cannot get a connection already did, instead of 500. SQLSTATE class 08 (except 08P01), 57P01, 57P02, 57P03 and 57P05, and a reset, aborted or closed socket on an open session count as such a cut (#4290).

  • While PostgreSQL is down, requests that need the database answer 503 with Retry-After about a second after the first one starts waiting, and at once after that, instead of each queueing up to db.acquire_timeout_secs (30 seconds by default). An acquire that has waited a second tries one connection of its own; when that cannot reach the database, the outage is known until a fresh attempt connects, and requests are served again as soon as one does. A pool that is only busy keeps queueing as before (#4323).

  • Superseding a composition or a party no longer slows down as its history grows. The foreign-key check that every new node and attestation row makes against its version could scan all versions of the object instead of probing one, depending on the planner statistics at the time: on the storage bench, superseding an object with a few hundred versions took about 14 ms instead of 9 ms when the plan flipped. Migrations clinical/0022 and party/0013 re-key the version-tree uniqueness constraint uq_version_tree with the object id last, so the check always probes the primary key. The constraint enforces the same uniqueness as before (#4340).

  • The FHIR rendering of an access record ehds-logging does not classify (a template upload, a stored-query write, a template read) now carries the IHE BALP 1.1.4 entity:data slice its Create, Read, Update or Delete profile requires: type 2, role 4 and what.identifier, naming the operation when the record names no object. HAPI FHIR’s validator refused the template upload record without it (#4353).

  • A + in a query string is a literal plus, as RFC 3986 §2.1 and §3.4 decode a URI query, on every ITS-REST operation and every extension route: a date-time offset such as 2026-10-28T10:00:00+01:00 or an AQL parameter sent with an unencoded + reaches the server unchanged, where it was read as a space. A space in a query value is sent as %20. This reverses the form-decoding of #3891: a client that writes a space as + now sends a plus. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.114 (#4356).

  • An AQL EHR e[ehr_id/value='…'] predicate whose value is not a UUID ('1234', the AQL 1.1.0 example) answers an empty result, as its WHERE e/ehr_id/value = '…' spelling does, on POST and GET /query/aql; it was refused with 400. Both spellings lower the EHR id comparison through one path, and a value the database cannot cast is refused with a message that no longer claims it came from a query parameter (#4378).

  • An AQL query with an archetype predicate no longer builds the archetype index bitmap of the whole store once per version. The planner multiplied the selectivities of the archetype columns, which each archetype fixes together, and expected about 15 000 of 545 067 blood-pressure OBSERVATIONs; a query over one EHR then took 38.8 s and answered 408. Clinical migration 0021_archetype_statistics.sql gives the columns a statistics object, and the same query takes 0.3 s (#4399).

  • FROM PERSON p CONTAINS EHR e (and the ORGANISATION and ROLE roots) joins a party to the EHR whose EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref names it, so a party created with POST /demographic/person and an EHR created with POST /ehr answer their row with no other call. Before, the join read only the party-to-EHR map, which no REST route writes, and answered no rows on a deployed server. The reference matches when its id.value is the party’s uid without ::<system>::<version> and its type is the root class or its RM ancestor (ACTOR, PARTY), in any namespace; an EHR linked both ways answers once (#4411).

  • An AQL projection whose path ends on a list attribute inside a node’s data (c/feeder_audit/originating_system_item_ids, c/links, c/context/participations, c/composer/identifiers, .../mappings) answers the list itself, [{…}, {…}], and null when the list is absent. It answered the list wrapped in a second list, [[{…}, {…}]]; a client that unwrapped that outer array reads the column directly now. A path that continues below a list (.../originating_system_item_ids/id) still answers the array of its matches, ["…", "…"]. COUNT over a path ending on a list counts its elements (#4413).

  • Reading one version of a composition, EHR_STATUS, folder or party by its version id no longer slows down as the object’s history grows. Once a connection reused its prepared read, the plan scanned every version of the object and kept the one asked for: on the storage bench’s history of 500 versions such a read touched about 520 buffers instead of 12 to 24. Migrations clinical/0023 and party/0014 add an index on the version tree id columns of both storage tiers, so the read probes the one version it returns (#4420).

  • An audit store that 5.6.0-rc2 migrated starts again. Audit migration 0017 changed after 5.6.0-rc2 shipped it, so the server refused such a store on the migration’s checksum at boot. 0017 is back to its 5.6.0-rc2 text, and the new audit migration 0019_search_tokens_pending_list.sql gives the search token index its pending list of 512 kB, so a store that 5.6.0-rc2 migrated upgrades in place (#4424).

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: both fixes exist only in ferrohealth-server releases that carry functional changes in the same serving path beside them (0.3.7 two fixes, 0.3.8 and 0.3.9 the problem details module, the kept listener TLS and the unmasked remedy), so there is no security-only release of the crate for FerroEHR to take, and the client CA refusal ships in the release candidate the advisory names.

  • FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.7 in place of 0.3.5 (GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg). Every earlier release held a plain-HTTP connection that never sent a byte for as long as the client kept it open, so about 8400 silent connections from a client with no credentials exhausted the quickstart’s file descriptors and the CDR stopped answering, health checks included; the listener then retried a failed accept at once and logged every failure. Such a connection now closes once [server] header_read_timeout_ms passes (30 s by default), counted from accept, and after an EMFILE or ENFILE the listener pauses up to 1 s before it accepts again and logs one warning every 10 seconds (#4283).

  • A [server.tls] table that sets client_ca_file with client_auth at none, written or by default, is refused at load, naming the setting (GHSA-52mf-qg39-4q4j). Before 5.5.0 a client CA alone meant that every client presents a certificate; 5.5.0 moved the listener onto ferrohealth-server, where client_auth defaults to none and the CA was read and ignored, so a configuration carried over passed config check and served without asking a client certificate. FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.9, which refuses it and names the remedy in full. A 5.5.0 deployer who sets client_ca_file sets client_auth = "required" beside it. The default template no longer pairs a client CA with none, and says what each client_auth value does (#4349).

5.6.0-rc2 - 2026-10-29

5.6.0-rc2 is the second release candidate of 5.6.0, published for testing. 5.6.0-rc1 was tagged but not published: the release plan refused it because its section missed a change merged just before the cut (#4361), so these notes carry every change since 5.5.0, those of the 5.6.0-rc1 section below included. 5.5.0 stays the stable release: this pre-release moves neither the latest image tags, the book under /docs/latest/ nor the hosted sandbox, it publishes no crates, and it receives no fixes; the next release candidate or 5.6.0 itself replaces it. Before you try it: every route ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define moves from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/ to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/, and the ITI-81 retrieval to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent, with no redirect from the old paths; audit migration 0017 refuses an audit store that holds records written by an earlier release, so point the release candidate at an empty audit store; a [server.tls] table with client_ca_file must set client_auth = "required" (or "optional") beside it, or the configuration is refused at load; and Helm chart 21.0.0-rc2 refuses to render until config.deployment_profile names sandbox or production. Storage generation 3 adds node columns and migrates no data, and clinical migration 0020 adds the origin to retention policies. Helm chart 21.0.0-rc2 carries appVersion 5.6.0-rc2. Security carries two advisories, GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg and GHSA-52mf-qg39-4q4j.

Added

  • The logging component’s intended performance is stated as checkable claims (EHDS Annex II 1.1): every composition create and read recorded exactly once and every AQL execution at least once, no access succeeding without its record, at most 125 % of the latency and at least 80 % of the throughput with the access log off, and a 50-record ITI-81 page within 250 ms at p95. scripts/perf/audit.sh measures them with the access log off and on (the load test’s new --audit mode counts the records through ITI-81 and times retrievals), scripts/perf/audit-verdict.sh gives the verdict, the release refuses a claim not met and attaches the summary as ferroehr-<tag>-logging-performance.md (Annex III point 2), and the weekly performance guard runs it on main. The book’s compliance section gains the page that states the claims and the method (#4293).

  • scripts/interop/atna.sh exercises the logging component’s ATNA transactions against independent implementations run from published images (EHDS Annex II 1.4): the ITI-20 FHIR feed into HAPI FHIR as the Audit Record Repository, judged by its validator with IHE BALP 1.1.4; the ITI-20 syslog feed into syslog-ng over RFC 5425 TLS, each payload read as a DICOM PS3.15 AuditMessage; and the same ITI-81 searches put to FerroEHR and to HAPI. The audit trail page documents it (#4296).

  • FerroEHR ships an EHDS category map for the published CKM templates and COMPOSITION archetypes whose data sit in one Art. 14(1) priority category (the International Patient Summary, ePrescription, the generic laboratory result and CCTA report templates; the health_summary, prescription and transfer_summary archetypes), so an installation that declares no [audit.categories] keys records those accesses classified instead of unclassified (EHDS Annex II 3.2(c)). A deployment that declares any template or archetype replaces it whole. [audit.categories] shipped_map = false with nothing declared leaves no map, which deployment_profile = "production" refuses as the new no_category_map gap unless deployment_accepts names it (#4298).

  • Retention periods and access rules can take the origin and the category of the data into account (EHDS Annex II 3.4). The new top-level [origins] register declares the origins a deployment recognises, each by the id its data carry and the clients whose direct commits come from it; a body without a FEEDER_AUDIT committed by a registered client is stamped with that client’s origin instead of the server’s system_id. PUT /admin/retention/policy takes an optional origin naming a registered origin, the register and GET /admin/retention/due report it, and the due list lists an origin-keyed period over the objects of that origin (clinical migration 0020_retention_by_origin.sql). The ABAC request carries category (the access record’s category tokens) and origin resource attributes on composition, contribution and query operations, the Cedar schema declares both, and a remote PDP binding may name them as parameters (#4299).

Changed

  • The Helm chart, at a new major version (21), has no default deployment profile: it refuses to render until config.deployment_profile names sandbox or production, so an installation that follows a quickstart instead of the instructions for use no longer runs the sandbox posture by omission (EHDS Annex II 1.2). A values file that relied on the old sandbox default must now set it, for example --set config.deployment_profile=sandbox; values-production.yaml sets production as before. The server binary’s own default and the Compose files, which declare sandbox explicitly, are unchanged (#4294).

  • The audit store keeps each record’s facts in columns and renders its FHIR R4 AuditEvent from them when the record is read over ITI-81 or delivered by the FHIR feed, instead of storing the rendered document in every record. A record takes about a quarter of the space it took before. The configuration the rendering depends on (the audit source, the store horizon, the category map and the emergency purposes) is kept once per distinct configuration in audit.audit_render_policy, and every record names the policy it was written under, so it renders the same document after the configuration changes. The tamper chain hashes every column of the record in one digest and checks each render policy against its digest; the earlier digest versions are retired. Audit migration 0017 needs an empty audit store and refuses one that holds records written by an earlier release, naming the remedy. ITI-81 parameters on an element of the document (address, the .identifier parameters, entity-type, entity-role, type, subtype) are matched against the rendered document (#4300).

  • The three audit indexes on recorded_at ascend, so their pages fill instead of splitting half full on every insert; the newest-first ITI-81 search scans them backward (#4302).

  • A clinical or party node row now stores only the part of its canonical JSON fragment that its own columns do not hold: _type, a lowercase archetype_node_id, a plain or simply coded name, and an ELEMENT value in one of the common basic shapes (a quantity, count, ordinal, coded or plain text, date, time, duration, identifier, boolean or URI) move into columns, the value into the new typed value columns. Every reader rebuilds the omitted keys, so the canonical JSON and every AQL result are unchanged, and a filter on a quantity’s magnitude or a code reads its column directly. The node heap shrinks by about a third (storage generation 3); a row written before keeps its whole fragment and reads the same. Migrations ext/0005, clinical/0019 and party/0012 add the columns and the readers; no data is migrated (#4306).

  • Every ITI-81 search parameter answers through an index again. The store takes the search tokens of a record’s rendered AuditEvent when it writes the record: each distinct token once in audit.audit_search_token, the code-system tokens (type, subtype, entity-type, entity-role, source.identifier) as one shared set in audit.audit_search_set, and their ids on the record in search_tokens under a GIN index; entity reads a hash index on resource_id. A search on address or a token parameter no longer renders every record in its date window. The tamper chain covers search_tokens, and the verifier reports a changed token or set (#4313).

  • Nothing ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define is served under the openEHR base path any more. FerroEHR serves three namespaces beside each other under /ferroehr/rest/: /openehr/v1/ holds only the ITS-REST routes, /fhir/r4/ the FHIR and IHE interfaces, and /extensions/v1/ FerroEHR’s own extensions. The ITI-81 retrieval moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/fhir/r4/AuditEvent to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent. These routes moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/... to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/... with the same relative path: /terminology/..., /admin/event_subscription..., /demographic/party_relationship..., /demographic/versioned_party_relationship/..., /definition/archetype/..., /definition/artefact/..., /message/export..., /message/import..., /query/cohort, and the admin extensions /admin/config, /admin/template/{template_id}, /admin/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version}, /admin/party/..., /admin/archive/..., /admin/report/..., /admin/dump, /admin/load, /admin/integrity/..., /admin/restriction..., /admin/access-restriction..., /admin/research-objection and /admin/retention/.... The old paths answer 404, with no redirect. The served OpenAPI document and its family documents name the new paths; the admin extensions, the archetype library and the cohort query have family documents of their own (admin-extensions, archetypes, cohort, contributions). The paged CONTRIBUTION list moved too, to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution (#4330).

  • The server and viewer images build on the current gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot digest, so they carry the base image’s latest Debian package updates (#4335).

  • Canonical JSON validation against the openEHR ITS-JSON schemas runs on jsonschema 0.59.0, which refuses a value whose regex match the engine cannot finish where 0.58 accepted it under not or patternProperties. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.113 (#4336).

  • A [server.tls] table that sets client_ca_file with client_auth at none, written or by default, is refused at load, naming the setting (GHSA-52mf-qg39-4q4j). Before 5.5.0 a client CA alone meant that every client presents a certificate; 5.5.0 moved the listener onto ferrohealth-server, where client_auth defaults to none and the CA was read and ignored, so a configuration carried over passed config check and served without asking a client certificate. FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.9, which refuses it and names the remedy in full. A 5.5.0 deployer who sets client_ca_file sets client_auth = "required" beside it. The default template no longer pairs a client CA with none, and says what each client_auth value does (#4349).

5.6.0-rc1 - 2026-10-28

5.6.0-rc1 is the first release candidate of 5.6.0, published for testing. 5.5.0 stays the stable release: this pre-release moves neither the latest image tags, the book under /docs/latest/ nor the hosted sandbox, it publishes no crates, and it receives no fixes; the next release candidate or 5.6.0 itself replaces it. Before you try it: every route ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define moves from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/ to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/, and the ITI-81 retrieval to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent, with no redirect from the old paths; and audit migration 0017 refuses an audit store that holds records written by an earlier release, so point the release candidate at an empty audit store. Storage generation 3 adds node columns and migrates no data. Helm chart 20.0.1-rc1 carries appVersion 5.6.0-rc1. Security carries one advisory, GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg.

Added

  • FerroEHR ships an EHDS category map for the published CKM templates and COMPOSITION archetypes whose data sit in one Art. 14(1) priority category (the International Patient Summary, ePrescription, the generic laboratory result and CCTA report templates; the health_summary, prescription and transfer_summary archetypes), so an installation that declares no [audit.categories] keys records those accesses classified instead of unclassified (EHDS Annex II 3.2(c)). A deployment that declares any template or archetype replaces it whole. [audit.categories] shipped_map = false with nothing declared leaves no map, which deployment_profile = "production" refuses as the new no_category_map gap unless deployment_accepts names it (#4298).

Changed

  • The audit store keeps each record’s facts in columns and renders its FHIR R4 AuditEvent from them when the record is read over ITI-81 or delivered by the FHIR feed, instead of storing the rendered document in every record. A record takes about a quarter of the space it took before. The configuration the rendering depends on (the audit source, the store horizon, the category map and the emergency purposes) is kept once per distinct configuration in audit.audit_render_policy, and every record names the policy it was written under, so it renders the same document after the configuration changes. The tamper chain hashes every column of the record in one digest and checks each render policy against its digest; the earlier digest versions are retired. Audit migration 0017 needs an empty audit store and refuses one that holds records written by an earlier release, naming the remedy. ITI-81 parameters on an element of the document (address, the .identifier parameters, entity-type, entity-role, type, subtype) are matched against the rendered document (#4300).

  • The three audit indexes on recorded_at ascend, so their pages fill instead of splitting half full on every insert; the newest-first ITI-81 search scans them backward (#4302).

  • A clinical or party node row now stores only the part of its canonical JSON fragment that its own columns do not hold: _type, a lowercase archetype_node_id, a plain or simply coded name, and an ELEMENT value in one of the common basic shapes (a quantity, count, ordinal, coded or plain text, date, time, duration, identifier, boolean or URI) move into columns, the value into the new typed value columns. Every reader rebuilds the omitted keys, so the canonical JSON and every AQL result are unchanged, and a filter on a quantity’s magnitude or a code reads its column directly. The node heap shrinks by about a third (storage generation 3); a row written before keeps its whole fragment and reads the same. Migrations ext/0005, clinical/0019 and party/0012 add the columns and the readers; no data is migrated (#4306).

  • Every ITI-81 search parameter answers through an index again. The store takes the search tokens of a record’s rendered AuditEvent when it writes the record: each distinct token once in audit.audit_search_token, the code-system tokens (type, subtype, entity-type, entity-role, source.identifier) as one shared set in audit.audit_search_set, and their ids on the record in search_tokens under a GIN index; entity reads a hash index on resource_id. A search on address or a token parameter no longer renders every record in its date window. The tamper chain covers search_tokens, and the verifier reports a changed token or set (#4313).

  • Nothing ITS-REST 1.1.0 does not define is served under the openEHR base path any more. FerroEHR serves three namespaces beside each other under /ferroehr/rest/: /openehr/v1/ holds only the ITS-REST routes, /fhir/r4/ the FHIR and IHE interfaces, and /extensions/v1/ FerroEHR’s own extensions. The ITI-81 retrieval moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/fhir/r4/AuditEvent to /ferroehr/rest/fhir/r4/AuditEvent. These routes moved from /ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1/... to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/... with the same relative path: /terminology/..., /admin/event_subscription..., /demographic/party_relationship..., /demographic/versioned_party_relationship/..., /definition/archetype/..., /definition/artefact/..., /message/export..., /message/import..., /query/cohort, and the admin extensions /admin/config, /admin/template/{template_id}, /admin/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version}, /admin/party/..., /admin/archive/..., /admin/report/..., /admin/dump, /admin/load, /admin/integrity/..., /admin/restriction..., /admin/access-restriction..., /admin/research-objection and /admin/retention/.... The old paths answer 404, with no redirect. The served OpenAPI document and its family documents name the new paths; the admin extensions, the archetype library and the cohort query have family documents of their own (admin-extensions, archetypes, cohort, contributions). The paged CONTRIBUTION list moved too, to /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/ehr/{ehr_id}/contribution (#4330).

  • The server and viewer images build on the current gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot digest, so they carry the base image’s latest Debian package updates (#4335).

  • Canonical JSON validation against the openEHR ITS-JSON schemas runs on jsonschema 0.59.0, which refuses a value whose regex match the engine cannot finish where 0.58 accepted it under not or patternProperties. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.113 (#4336).

Fixed

  • The hosted sandbox seeds its full demo dataset again. The v5.5.0 reseed stopped at the ADL 2 archetype library (233 stored / 89 refused against the pinned 231 / 91) because the box’s .env still forced FerroTERM 0.1.6, which reads none of the FerroTERM 0.3 settings the sandbox posture passes, so it served no LOINC and VETDF could only warn on braden_scale’s mistyped LA9605-4. The corpus, the pin and the CDR were right. The seed now asks the CDR for a LOINC code before the library step and names a posture without LOINC (SANDBOX_TERMINOLOGY=without-loinc opts a local run into 233 / 89), checks that the two files it names move together, and a corpus test holds the manifest’s pin to the adjudicated split with and without LOINC. The FerroPIX rollout script retires a stale FERROTERM_IMAGE override, checks that FerroTERM runs the pinned version and serves LOINC, and wipes before it seeds over an unfinished seed (#4278).

  • A response to a request whose body FerroEHR left unread, such as a 404 to a POST of a path it does not serve or a declared-length 413, now carries Connection: close. The connection closed after such a response without saying so, and a client that sent its next request on it met a closed socket, which a non-idempotent request cannot safely retry (RFC 9112 §9.6) (#4283).

  • A [server.caller_rate] above 1 000 000 000 requests per second no longer answers 429 to concurrent requests: such a rate now limits nothing, as its operator meant (#4283).

  • Every request leaves one request line, a timeout 408, a declared-length 413 and the 500 of a panicked handler included, and a 413 for a body with no declared length that passes [server] body_limit_bytes is answered with the openEHR error body, as the declared-length 413 is (#4283).

  • An AQL query whose WHERE clause chains thousands of NOT, AND or OR terms no longer overflows the stack and aborts the server. The parser refuses a query that nests brackets and CONTAINS deeper than 64 levels or builds an expression deeper than 512 levels with 400 Bad Request, before any recursive pass runs, on the ad-hoc, stored-query store and execution paths alike. A long OR over one path is written as MATCHES {…}, which the bound does not count. A statement PostgreSQL refuses for its own complexity limit (SQLSTATE class 54) also answers 400 instead of 500. openehr-query gains ParseError::TooDeep (#4284).

  • An AQL query (ad hoc or stored) whose client disconnects, or that the server’s own query.timeout_ms or HTTP request timeout gives up on, no longer keeps its statement running and its pooled connection busy until the statement ends. The connection is closed instead of returned to the pool, so the slot frees at once, and every pooled session now sets PostgreSQL’s client_connection_check_interval to one second, so the backend stops the abandoned statement within about a second. The composition-count statistics behave the same way (#4285).

  • The server’s resident memory no longer climbs under sustained load until the container’s memory limit kills it. The ferroehr binary now allocates through mimalloc instead of glibc malloc, whose per-thread arenas kept freed memory and never gave it back. On a load test of 10 000 mixed jobs at 48 workers the peak resident set fell from 2.3 to 3.2 GB (growing run after run) to about 600 MB, and throughput rose by about a third (#4288).

  • A request whose database connection a PostgreSQL restart, a crash or the network cuts now answers 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After, as a request that cannot get a connection already did, instead of 500. SQLSTATE class 08 (except 08P01), 57P01, 57P02, 57P03 and 57P05, and a reset, aborted or closed socket on an open session count as such a cut (#4290).

  • While PostgreSQL is down, requests that need the database answer 503 with Retry-After about a second after the first one starts waiting, and at once after that, instead of each queueing up to db.acquire_timeout_secs (30 seconds by default). An acquire that has waited a second tries one connection of its own; when that cannot reach the database, the outage is known until a fresh attempt connects, and requests are served again as soon as one does. A pool that is only busy keeps queueing as before (#4323).

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: the fix exists only in ferrohealth-server 0.3.7, which carries two functional fixes in the same serving path beside it, so there is no security-only release of the crate for FerroEHR to take.

  • FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-server 0.3.7 in place of 0.3.5 (GHSA-2mc2-h3jq-c5wg). Every earlier release held a plain-HTTP connection that never sent a byte for as long as the client kept it open, so about 8400 silent connections from a client with no credentials exhausted the quickstart’s file descriptors and the CDR stopped answering, health checks included; the listener then retried a failed accept at once and logged every failure. Such a connection now closes once [server] header_read_timeout_ms passes (30 s by default), counted from accept, and after an EMFILE or ENFILE the listener pauses up to 1 s before it accepts again and logs one warning every 10 seconds (#4283).

5.5.0 - 2026-10-27

5.5.0 moves the server and the viewer onto the FerroHEALTH family’s shared configuration, HTTP, telemetry, authorization and audit crates, and it carries breaking changes for every deployment, each with its upgrade step under Changed or Removed. Before you upgrade: name the configuration file with FERROEHR_CONFIG (or --config), since ./ferroehr.toml and /etc/ferroehr/ferroehr.toml are no longer searched; move the REST keys from [server] to [rest] and rename server.bind to server.listen; move [authz.rbac] role_claims and [authz.rbac.basic_roles] to [auth] role_claims and each [[auth.basic.users]] roles, and remove user_role; rename token_url to token_endpoint in the outbound OAuth tables; remove [audit.fhir_feed] batch_size, max_retries and [usage_report] slow_aql_ms; list a reverse proxy in [server] trusted_proxies; and give the viewer server.listen in place of LEPTOS_SITE_ADDR. The server refuses to start without a patient identity source for its EHR index unless [ehr_index] provider = "local" is set, ITI-81 audit retrieval requires a date parameter, and Template Data Document import is gone. Helm chart 20.0.0 carries appVersion 5.5.0. Security carries two advisories, GHSA-vphj-3f8c-5hpx and GHSA-cwhv-87pq-3c3c.

Added

  • The access record names the data permit a secondary-use caller acts under (#3379). A caller declares the permit’s identifier in the header [audit] permit_header names (default x-data-permit) beside its purpose of use; every access record keeps it as permit, so the trail says under which permit a population query, an export or a cohort query ran (EHDS Art. 68). A value that is not 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : / # - is recorded as absent. The column joins the tamper chain as digest version 4 (audit migration 0016). The FHIR rendering carries it too (#4120).

  • AQL takes VERSIONED_OBJECT as a FROM class (#3379), the shape of FerroBRIDGE’s OMOP batch query (EHR e CONTAINS VERSIONED_OBJECT vo CONTAINS VERSION v CONTAINS COMPOSITION c). The QUERY specification lets FROM name any RM class (master03 §FROM), and FerroEHR refused this one. The variable answers uid/value and owner_id/id/value (RM common master06 §VERSIONED_OBJECT) and refuses any other path. The operand sets no version scope of its own.

  • The book records the secondary-use contract with FerroBRIDGE (#3379). The new Secondary use page states the batch query FerroBRIDGE loads the OMOP CDM from (time_committed > $since, ordered by the commit instant and the version uid, paged by offset and fetch), the marks that take an EHR out of a batch, the reconciliation that removes erased compositions, and where pseudonymisation for research happens. An integration test holds the batch to it. The compliance overview no longer names the withdrawn secondary-use read model (#3160) as planned.

  • The EHR index asks an IHE patient identity source over PIXm (ITI-83) by default (#3380). [ehr_index] provider = "ihe" names a PIX Manager by its FHIR base (pixm_url) and the clinical domain (assigning_authority, one of privacy.subject_namespaces), with the client credentials grant of [ehr_index.oauth] (renewed once on a 401) and the TLS material of [ehr_index.tls] (trust_roots_file, client_identity_file, min_version). The client is ihe-iti 0.0.62’s PIXm Consumer and sends only what ITI-83 specifies, by POST unless invocation = "get", so any conformant PIX Manager serves. has_ehr_for_subject and create_ehr_for_subject ask the source for the subject’s pseudonym, and the subjects of an EHR are the pseudonym its EHR_STATUS carries; the source is never asked to resolve a pseudonym back. The server reads the source’s CapabilityStatement at boot, and a source that fails a request is an error: nothing falls back to the in-instance map. PDQm is not used (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).

  • The book states FerroEHR’s contract as a federation node (#3383). The new page “FerroEHR as a federation node” reads the openEHR Federation Tier with AQL 1.0.0 from the node’s side. It lists the endpoints a gateway uses and resolution by the local ehr_id alone. It gives the four admission conditions of N42a and the configuration that meets them: a unique system_id, and an import under an ehr_id the node chose. It also covers authentication by the deployment’s own authorization server and the refusals the node applies whatever the gateway did. It names FerroFED 0.0.13 as the release whose harness runs FerroEHR as its node. An integration test moves an EHR between two nodes under a node-chosen id and finds every version uid and its creating_system_id unchanged.

  • The FLAT builder builds an INTERVAL_EVENT at an abstract EVENT node when the input names its width (#3898), on the 0.0.102 crate line. RM data_structures §EVENT makes EVENT abstract over POINT_EVENT and INTERVAL_EVENT, and a /width, /math_function or |sample_count under such a node (master05 §INTERVAL_EVENT) now chooses the interval; without them the node still builds as a POINT_EVENT. The flattener writes those rows back for an interval event held at an abstract node.

  • The audit store deletes each record at its own retention end (#3899). Every record stores the first date it may be deleted on: an access record the end ehds-logging states for its categories and origins (Regulation (EU) 2025/327 Annex II 3.4), any other record the day after its date of access plus the [audit.store] horizon, and none for a record kept without end. The reaper deletes a record on or after that date and never before it, where it deleted by one store-wide horizon. Records written before this release keep the horizon. The end joins the chain digest (version 3), so moving one shows in the chain check.

  • The viewer trusts a private CA for the CDR and the OIDC issuer on every platform: [cdr.tls] and [auth.oidc.tls] take trust_roots_file, a PEM bundle trusted beside the platform’s roots, with client_identity (_file) for mutual TLS and min_version, read through ferrohealth_server::tls_client. A file that cannot be read or holds no certificate refuses the start. The Helm chart names the CDR’s CA through cdr.tls.trust_roots_file in place of SSL_CERT_DIR, and viewer.auth.oidc.caExistingSecret mounts an issuer CA; the UI journeys pass the development Keycloak CA the same way (#3909).

  • Opaque access tokens are checked by token introspection under [auth] mode = "introspection" (#4033). ferrohealth-smart’s introspection check (RFC 7662) posts each bearer token to the issuer’s introspection endpoint, named by its metadata or by [auth.introspection] endpoint, and authenticates as the client of [auth.introspection.client] or with the token of [auth.introspection.bearer]. An active response admits the caller with its scopes and roles and is reused until its exp, an inactive token is a 401, and an endpoint that cannot answer is a 503. The mode and the table were refused at boot. Helm chart 15.1.0 names the mode.

  • The ITI-81 audit retrieval applies every search parameter RESTful ATNA §3.81.4.1.2.2 says the repository shall support (#4040): address, agent.identifier, patient.identifier, entity.identifier, entity-type, entity-role, source.identifier, type, subtype and outcome, beside patient, agent, entity and action. Several comma-separated values match any of them, and a repeated parameter must match too. Tokens take the code, |code and system|code forms of FHIR R4 Search §3.1.1.4.10. These parameters were a 400 not-supported. The subject-scoped audit role still names exactly one subject, by patient or patient.identifier.

  • The openehr-* crates carry the APIs FerroBRIDGE kept local copies of (#4047, #4048), on the 0.0.99 crate line. The FLAT builder takes a value whole under |raw (Simplified Formats master04 §Raw canonical JSON) on ROLE.performer (<root>/performer|raw, a PARTY_REF), on the COMPOSITION language, territory and composer, and on the _feeder_audit, _link:i, _participation:i, _other_participation:i, _provider and _health_care_facility families. A ctx/ key still wins over a path spelling of the same attribute, and a raw value of the wrong class, or one beside another suffix, is refused as InvalidRaw. openehr-am implements FromStr for ArchetypeHrid (openehr_adl::hrid::parse_hrid now reads through it), openehr-base adds TerminologyId::new(name, version_id), and openehr-term names the audit_change_type and version_lifecycle_state concepts (codes::AuditChangeType, codes::VersionLifecycleState), held equal to the embedded terminology. Until a ferrohealth-smart release requires 0.0.99, the build holds a registry copy of openehr-sdt 0.0.98 for it beside the workspace 0.0.99.

  • An ADL 2 Web Template names a node under a template overlay by its parent archetype. openehr_adl::opt::create_opt records each overlay’s specialisation parent in the OPT’s other_meta_data (template_overlay_parents), and the ADL 2 builder uses the parent’s id for the node, its paths and its slot admissions, so data and mappings written against the published archetype match. An ADL 2 header now quotes a free metadata value that is not a bare token and reads a quoted one back (#4048).

  • TEMPLATE_ID answers its BASE 1.3.0 HRID functions (#4068), on the 0.0.104 crate line. SPECBASE-42 gives TEMPLATE_ID is_hrid, namespace, qualified_rm_class_name, concept_id, version_id and the major, minor and patch versions (BASE base_types master05 §Template Identifiers). An identifier in the namespaced HRID form of the Artefact Identification reference expression (master03 §Formal Model) yields its parts; a legacy free-text template name stays valid and answers false and empty parts.

  • openehr-its writes an OPT 1.4, on the 0.0.105 crate line: opt14_writer::build and write assemble an operational template from a template definition (the root archetype, the archetypes placed in its slots or open attributes, and the occurrences, existences and attribute constraints it narrows) and the AM 1.4 archetypes it names. Internal references are inlined and deleted nodes removed (OPT2 raw flattening), a slot filler is checked against the slot’s assertions and type, a widening is refused, and the output is byte-deterministic, valid against ITS-XML Template.xsd and accepted by the template upload (#4083).

  • The server runs the FerroHEALTH HTTP stack of ferrohealth-server 0.3.4, and [server] is its section, the same keys in every FerroHEALTH product: listen, base_path (a path every route is served under, the health routes included; empty by default), request_timeout_ms (a request still running is answered 408), header_read_timeout_ms, body_limit_bytes, drain_delay_ms and shutdown_timeout_ms (on SIGTERM readiness turns 503 at once, the listener closes after the delay, and the requests in flight get the bound to finish), max_concurrent_requests with retry_after_s, trusted_proxies with forwarded_header, and compression with compression_min_bytes. [server.caller_rate] (requests_per_second, burst) limits each authenticated caller. [server.tls] (certificate_file, key_file, client_auth, client_ca_file, min_version, reload_interval_s, healthcheck_identity_file) reads the files again on SIGHUP too, and the management listener on its own port drains with the main one under the same bound (#4087).

  • [rest] holds the openEHR REST surface: base_path, swagger_ui, cors_permissive, system_id, [rest.identity] and body_limit_bytes, the clinical body tier below server.body_limit_bytes, which the template-upload and /message routes keep (#4087).

  • ferroehr serve names the default command beside config check and healthcheck (#4087).

  • The viewer serves the family’s health routes and commands: /health/liveness, /health/readiness and /health, ferroehr-viewer config check (reads the configuration and builds the CDR and issuer clients without reaching either), --config and --set key=value, the [server] table with listener TLS, and the bounded drain on SIGTERM (server.drain_delay_ms, server.shutdown_timeout_ms). ferroehr-viewer with no subcommand still serves (#4139).

  • The OPT 1.4 writer clones nodes and narrows types, on the 0.0.106 crate line: opt14_writer::Narrowing::Clone copies an archetype node that may occur more than once under its own node id, told apart by a name constraint and carrying its own narrowings and slot fills, and refuses a clone of a node that occurs at most once, a name another copy carries, or copies the attribute’s cardinality cannot hold (AOM2 VSONCO, VACMCU, VACMCO). Narrowing::Redefine narrows an attribute’s children to conforming subtypes (a DV_TEXT value to a DV_CODED_TEXT) or drops alternatives, keeping the archetype’s other constraints, and refuses a type that does not conform (AOM2 VSONCT). An attribute the template constrains can also hold archetypes placed by a slot fill. The writer now rebuilds 143 of the 305 CKM operational templates to their upstream node tree, up from 67 (#4150).

  • The OPT 1.4 writer refuses a redefined leaf constraint that admits a value the archetype’s does not, as AOM2 Phase 2 validation (VPOV) requires: a string list or pattern, an integer or real list or range, a boolean, a date, time, date/time or duration range, pattern or timezone validity, a code phrase’s terminology or code list, a quantity’s property, units, magnitude or precision, and an ordinal list. Each refusal is a WriteError::Widening naming the archetype, the path and the constraint. The openehr crates move to 0.0.107 (#4163).

  • The Helm chart mounts a private issuer CA for the server: auth.caExistingSecret (with auth.caExistingSecretKey, ca.crt by default) mounts the Secret’s PEM bundle and points the server’s [auth] ca_file at it, as viewer.auth.oidc.caExistingSecret does for the viewer. Chart 19.3.0 (#4235).

  • The quickstart viewer signs in through the Keycloak overlay: with --profile viewer, the viewer at http://localhost:3000 takes the authorization-code flow with PKCE through the demo realm’s ferroehr-viewer client and calls the server with the user’s token. The issuer moves to https://keycloak.localhost:8443, a name the containers resolve through a network alias and a browser resolves to the loopback address with no hosts entry, and the development certificate names it (#4243).

Changed

  • A server with no patient identity source refuses to start (#3380). The binary’s default [ehr_index] provider is the IHE one, and without pixm_url and assigning_authority the refusal names both choices: configure the identity source, or opt in to the in-instance map with [ehr_index] provider = "local", which serves the GET /ehr?subject_id=… lookup over EHR_STATUS content and nothing more. Upgrade step: a deployment without an identity source adds [ehr_index] provider = "local" (FERROEHR__EHR_INDEX__PROVIDER=local).

  • The compose quickstart runs FerroPIX beside FerroEHR (#3380), pinned by tag and digest, with its own PostgreSQL and a development OpenID Provider, and points [ehr_index] at it; FerroPIX mints the pseudonym in urn:oid:2.999.7.1 on FerroEHR’s first ask. The server now runs in the issuer’s network namespace, which publishes ports 8080, 8090 (FERROEHR_PIX_PORT) and 8180 (FERROEHR_ISSUER_PORT).

  • Helm chart 19.0.0 takes FerroPIX as the chart dependency ferropix (#3380), on by default: the chart points config.ehr_index at its Service, adds the egress rule to its pods, and routes the grant’s client secret through secrets.ehrIndexClientSecret. A values file that names no identity source is refused at render. Upgrade step: supply FerroPIX’s ferropix.database.existingSecret, ferropix.dataKey.existingSecret, its issuer and pseudonymisation domain, and config.ehr_index, or set ferropix.enabled: false with config.ehr_index.provider: local.

  • The EHDS system documents live in the FerroHEALTH book, and each release attaches them at a pinned revision (#3705). The EHR system Cadasto B.V. declares is FerroEHR with FerroBRIDGE, so its information sheet (EHDS Art. 38), instructions for use (Art. 30(1)(d)), readiness record and technical documentation (Art. 37, Annex III) move to https://ferrohealth.eu/docs/ehds/, and the old addresses in this book redirect there. docs/ehds/system-documents.env pins the FerroHEALTH commit and the revision of each page. The release lane fetches the two attached pages at that commit, refuses a page whose Revised line differs from the pin, and appends this release’s facts under “This copy”: the system version (this FerroEHR release with the FerroBRIDGE release its chart runs beside), the release date and the versions of the standards, read from docs/VERSIONS.md (Art. 38(2)(b) and (e)). The release notes name the pinned revisions, and release-notes.sh refuses notes that do not.

  • Breaking: the XML readers of openehr-its refuse a document outside the schema (#3893), on the 0.0.103 crate line. A child element a type’s closed xs:sequence does not declare, or a child element inside a text element, is refused with XmlError::UndeclaredChild (XML Schema 1.1 Part 1 §3.4.4.2) where it was skipped as if absent, and opt14::from_xml and the AOM2 readers refuse a root other than the one the schema publishes (<template>, ITS-XML components/AM/Release-1.4/Template.xsd) with XmlError::UnexpectedRoot. One tool-written element no schema declares, match_negated on a C_ATTRIBUTE, is read when false and refused when true (XmlError::UnsupportedExtension): a negated match changes the constraint, and no schema says how. A CDR upload of a template outside the schema is now refused; the CNF Robot valid_templates/validation/clinical_content_validation.opt and two epSOS CKM templates are such documents (#4077, #4078).

  • [auth] ca_file is trusted under introspection mode too: with ferrohealth-smart 0.8.6 the server reads an introspecting issuer’s metadata, and calls its introspection and token endpoints, trusting the bundle beside the platform roots and the grant’s own ca_file. The e2e compose overlay names the development Keycloak CA through FERROEHR__AUTH__CA_FILE in place of SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR (#3909).

  • The shared crates move to their newest lockstep releases: ferrohealth-smart 0.7.3, ferrohealth-authz 0.1.3, ihe-atna and ehds-logging 0.2.12 and ferrobridge-term 0.1.138. Every secret in the [auth] section now renders as ***, the family mask, and [auth] ca_file names a PEM bundle of extra certificate authorities for the issuer’s metadata and key set, for an issuer behind a private PKI (#3909).

  • Breaking: the audit trail believes a forwarded client address only from a trusted proxy (#4025). The source network address of an audit record (client_ip, the DICOM NetworkAccessPointID, the FHIR AuditEvent network) is the address the family server stack names: the connection’s peer, or the client a peer listed in [server] trusted_proxies names in the [server] forwarded_header (RFC 7239 §8.1). FerroEHR read the first X-Forwarded-For hop from any caller, so a client could write any address into the trail. A deployment behind a reverse proxy lists the proxy in trusted_proxies and sets forwarded_header = "x-forwarded-for" when the proxy does not send Forwarded; until then its records name the proxy.

  • FerroEHR moves to ferrohealth-usage-report 0.2.0 (#4025). The report FerroEHR sends is unchanged.

  • The CDR takes up ferrohealth-smart 0.6.0 and ferrobridge-term 0.1.134 (#4026, #4027). Token checking, Basic users, the discovery document and every outbound client credentials token behave as before. The terminology client now refuses, before sending, a code with no system on an STU3 server; the CDR’s server is R4B, so its binding checks are unchanged. The new [auth] mode = "introspection" key of the shared section, and an [auth.introspection] table, are refused at boot: this server checks bearer tokens as JWTs only, and a setting it would ignore stops the start.

  • Every secret and every masked URL renders through ferrohealth-secret, the family’s one mask (en-route finding of #4028). EHR’s own config::secret module gives way to ferrohealth-secret’s Secret, SecretUrl and RedactedUrl. A secret still renders as *** and a URL’s userinfo as ***@, and a URL’s query is now masked as ?*** too, in ferroehr config check, GET /admin/config, /management/env and ferroehr report. ferrohealth-smart moves to 0.7.1 and ferrohealth-authz to 0.1.1, ihe-atna and ehds-logging to 0.2.11, and ferrobridge-term to 0.1.137.

  • Breaking: the outbound client credentials tables take the ferrohealth-smart client table, so token_url is now token_endpoint (#4028). [terminology.server.oauth], [audit.fhir_feed.oauth] and [authz.abac.remote.oauth] are the family’s shared grant: the old key token_url stops startup by name, and each table gains private_key_jwt (RFC 7523), mutual TLS (tls_client_auth and self_signed_tls_client_auth, RFC 8705), ca_file, refresh_margin_ms and timeout_ms. issuer, client_id, the client secret, scope, audience and resource keep their names. Upgrade: rename token_url to token_endpoint in each table (in the Helm chart, under config.terminology.server.oauth and the other two), or ..._OAUTH__TOKEN_URL to ..._OAUTH__TOKEN_ENDPOINT in the environment. ferrohealth-smart moves to 0.7.0 and ihe-atna and ehds-logging to 0.2.10, the FHIR Feed sends its bearer token through ihe-atna, and every BALP AuditEvent’s source.observer carries an identifier beside its display.

  • Breaking: ihe-atna’s forwarder delivers the audit trail, and [audit.fhir_feed] batch_size and max_retries are gone (#4029). Syslog frames are stored in ihe-atna’s spool and delivered from it with backoff, retried until the repository takes them, so a failed send is no longer lost. The local audit store keeps only the FHIR document, so the spool, not the store, is syslog’s outbox, and delivered_syslog_at is no longer written. New [audit.syslog] keys: spool_dir (a spool that survives a restart; unset, it is held in memory), spool_max_messages, spool_max_bytes and retry_max_ms. The FHIR Feed delivers from the store through an ihe-atna outbox, or with the store off from an in-memory spool. A record the repository refuses is set aside until the next start, and the records behind it flow on. retry_max_ms takes the place of batch_size and max_retries, which stop startup by name. A new audit_delivery health indicator reports each forwarder. Upgrade: remove batch_size and max_retries from [audit.fhir_feed], and set [audit.syslog] spool_dir to a directory only the server can read.

  • Breaking: the ITI-81 audit retrieval (GET /fhir/r4/AuditEvent) requires a date parameter (#4030). The query is now read by ihe-atna’s retrieve, the family’s audit crate, and the answer written by it: RESTful ATNA §3.81.4.1.2.1 has at least one date present, so a query without one is a 400 OperationOutcome. A date value takes every FHIR prefix (eq when none, so date=2026-07-12 is that whole day, read in UTC), patient, agent and entity also answer to their .identifier forms, _count=0 returns the total alone, and the Bundle carries self and next links. A parameter the local store cannot apply yet is a 400 not-supported where it was silently ignored. Upgrade: an API client, a patient portal on the subject-scoped audit role included, adds a date window to every retrieval (for example date=ge2026-07-01); the viewer’s audit page sends the last 30 days when no window is set. ihe-atna and ehds-logging move to 0.2.8.

  • Breaking: [authz.rbac] user_role is retired (#4038 follow-up). It named a role nothing required once a Basic user’s roles became its [[auth.basic.users]] roles list. The key now stops startup by name and points at that list. Upgrade: remove user_role (on Helm chart 16.0.0, config.authz.rbac.user_role), and give each Basic user the roles it needs, for example roles = ["USER"].

  • Breaking: the caller’s roles come from ferrohealth-smart, so the two role keys move to [auth], and the policy decision is ferrohealth-authz 0.1.0 (#4038). [authz.rbac] role_claims is now [auth] role_claims (same default, realm_access.roles included), and [authz.rbac.basic_roles] is now the roles list of each [[auth.basic.users]] entry; both old places stop startup by name. Roles stay upper-cased, and a Basic user whose entry lists no role holds none, where a user absent from basic_roles used to hold user_role. [authz.assurance] and [authz.professional] keep their keys and are read by the shared sections; the RFC 9470 step-up challenge on patient data no longer carries an error_description. The Cedar engine and the remote decision point are the family’s: the Cedar schema and the remote wire body are unchanged, a remote resource kind with no policy is a 500 instead of a 403 (boot validation already refuses that configuration), and authz_cedar_decisions and authz_remote_pdp_calls count one per decision where they counted one per attribute combination. Upgrade: move role_claims from [authz.rbac] to [auth] (FERROEHR__AUTH__ROLE_CLAIMS in the environment), and each user’s entry of [authz.rbac.basic_roles] to roles under its [[auth.basic.users]] table (in the Helm chart, under config.auth.basic.users), and give a user that had no entry roles = ["USER"]. Helm chart 15.0.0 takes the same keys (config.auth.role_claims, roles under config.auth.basic.users, and token_endpoint in each grant). ferrobridge-term moves to 0.1.136, whose SmartToken replaces the terminology client’s own token adapter (#4031).

  • The openehr-rm tests take the change-type and lifecycle-state codes from openehr_term::codes (#4053), in the codegen templates of both generations, so no literal code or rubric can drift from the embedded terminology.

  • SECURITY.md records the main ruleset as it stands (#4067): no approving review, the conclusion check, the merge queue, and the organization-admin bypass, with what a bypass merge skips (any lane still running, ui-e2e included) and when it is used. The weekly external link check leaves out gesetze-im-internet.de and dicom.nema.org, which refuse the GitHub runner every week while answering by hand (#4074).

  • The BASE, AM, TERM and LANG specifications are re-vendored (#4068, #4069, #4070, #4071) at BASE 93abaf9f, AM 51aa07b2, TERM b2dd077d and LANG e61a7192. The TERM languages code set restores pt-pt, adds ro-md and ru-md, and names the replacement of each deprecated code (SPECTERM-36), so the openehr-term code-set lookup accepts the two new codes. The BASE Interval.has post-condition gains its brackets, which the implementation already followed. AM’s Archetype Identification document is superseded by BASE Artefact Identification (SPECAM-103), and the citations move with it. The nine openehr-* crates step to 0.0.104.

  • The bundled PostgreSQL image is rebuilt on the 2026-10-21 respin of postgres:18.6 (#4084, sha256:edb0c08d…), a same-version respin with rebuilt base packages. The respin ships the fixed xz packages, so the TEMP-1147318-639065 statement leaves security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json.

  • Breaking: the server reads only the configuration file it is told to read (#4087). The loader is ferrohealth-config 0.2.5, the FerroHEALTH products’ shared one, and it reads the file --config or FERROEHR_CONFIG names. ./ferroehr.toml and /etc/ferroehr/ferroehr.toml are no longer searched: a deployment that mounts a file there without naming it starts on the environment and the defaults alone. Set FERROEHR_CONFIG=/etc/ferroehr/ferroehr.toml; the Compose files, the conformance stacks and Helm chart 16.0.2 set it. The fallbacks keep their order (the libpq variables, DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, RUST_LOG, PORT), and ferroehr config check prints each key beside the source that set it.

  • Breaking: the viewer reads only the configuration file FERROEHR_VIEWER_CONFIG names (#4087), through the same ferrohealth-config loader as the CDR. ./ferroehr-viewer.toml and /etc/ferroehr/viewer.toml are no longer searched. A variable under FERROEHR_VIEWER_ that is neither an override nor the Compose port or image parameter refuses the start, and a *_file secret loses only its trailing line ending, where all surrounding whitespace was trimmed; an empty file is refused.

  • Breaking: [auth] role_claims defaults to ["roles", "groups", "entitlements"] (#4087), the RFC 9068 §2.2.3.1 carriers every FerroHEALTH product reads. realm_access.roles is no longer in the default: a Keycloak issuer sets FERROEHR__AUTH__ROLE_CLAIMS=roles,groups,entitlements,realm_access.roles, as the Keycloak Compose overlay and the viewer’s journey stack now do.

  • Breaking: the server no longer refuses a FERROEHR_ variable outside the override form, and a file refusal says less (#4087). Only a FERROEHR__<SECTION>__<KEY> override that names no key refuses the start. A single-_ spelling such as FERROEHR_DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS, or a per-subsystem pointer such as FERROEHR_SIGNING_CONFIG, sets nothing and is left alone, because the viewer’s FERROEHR_VIEWER_ variables share the prefix (ferrohealth-config 0.2.5). A refusal of an unknown key in the file names the key and the closest valid one, without its line number; a syntax error still names its line and column.

  • Breaking: /health/readiness and /management/health serve the FerroHEALTH readiness document of ferrohealth-health 0.1.1 (#4087). The body is {"state", "phase", "indicators": [{"name", "state", "detail"?}]} with lowercase states (up, degraded, down), replacing {"status", "components"}; the public probe leaves out every detail. Readiness also answers 503 while the process boots and from the moment it receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, before the listener stops. The optional indicators (audit_sender, audit_delivery, audit_chain, events) read at worst degraded, so a damaged audit chain now reads degraded where it read DOWN, and an indicator that is up carries no detail. The viewer’s health tab reads the same document. Probes that test only the status code are unaffected.

  • Breaking: logging, the request log and the OpenTelemetry export move to the [telemetry] section of ferrohealth-telemetry 0.2.1 (#4087), the FerroHEALTH products’ shared one, with no aliases for the old keys. [log] is gone: log.format and log.filter become telemetry.format and telemetry.filter (FERROEHR__TELEMETRY__FORMAT, FERROEHR__TELEMETRY__FILTER, RUST_LOG still a fallback), and the filter now defaults to info,hyper=warn,tower=warn,h2=warn and refuses the start when it does not parse. The export moves to a [telemetry.otlp] table: otlp_endpoint becomes otlp.endpoint, traces_sample_ratio becomes otlp.sample_ratio, and metrics_push becomes otlp.metrics, which defaults to true, so a configured endpoint now receives the metrics as well as the spans. telemetry.flame_file moves to management.flame_file. telemetry.service_name is removed: the service.name is always ferroehr. telemetry.environment no longer defaults to dev and is left off every span and metric unless set. A file or variable that still spells an old key refuses the start, naming it. Helm chart 17.0.0 renames config.log to config.telemetry.

  • Breaking: the HTTP metrics are the ferrohealth-telemetry request log’s (#4087). http_server_request_duration_seconds is labelled http_request_method, http_route, http_response_status_code and url_scheme (OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions); the status_class label is gone, so a query on status_class="5xx" becomes http_response_status_code=~"5..", as the bundled alert rules and Grafana dashboard now read. The http_server_active_requests, http_server_request_body_size and http_server_response_body_size series are removed, and no series on /management/prometheus carries the otel_scope_name label any more. The viewer’s management page loses its in-flight requests tile, and the dashboard’s in-flight panel shows the request rate.

  • Breaking: responses no longer carry x-trace-id, and a client’s traceparent is no longer read (#4087). Every request starts a trace of the server’s own, so a caller cannot join or steer the server’s traces; correlate a request through its x-request-id, which the request log writes on every line.

  • Breaking: the REST-surface keys move from [server] to [rest]: server.base_path, server.swagger_ui, server.cors_permissive, server.system_id and [server.identity] are rest.base_path, rest.swagger_ui, rest.cors_permissive, rest.system_id and [rest.identity] (FERROEHR__REST__…), with no alias; the old names are refused at startup. Upgrade: rename the keys, and move a [server.identity] table to [rest.identity] (#4087).

  • Breaking: server.bind is server.listen, an IP address and a port; a host name such as localhost:8080 refuses the start. It listens on 0.0.0.0:8080 by default, as before. Upgrade: rename the key (#4087).

  • Breaking: the request-body limit is server.body_limit_bytes, 64 MiB by default, the ceiling of every route and the limit of the template-upload and /message routes, and rest.body_limit_bytes (unset by default) narrows the other routes below it, where it was 16 MiB. The chart sets 16 MiB. Upgrade: set rest.body_limit_bytes = 16777216 to keep the old clinical limit (#4087).

  • Breaking: server.max_in_flight is server.max_concurrent_requests, unset (no bound) by default where it was 256, and the bound now covers every FerroEHR route (the status document, SMART discovery and the management surface included); only the health routes are never refused. Upgrade: set max_concurrent_requests = 256 to keep the old bound (#4087).

  • Breaking: [server.rate_limit] is [server.caller_rate] (requests_per_second, burst) keyed on the authenticated subject, and limits nobody until the table is set, where the principal tier was on by default; the per-address tier is gone. The chart and the Compose quickstart set 1024 per second with a burst of 2048. A 429 carries Retry-After and no x-ratelimit-* headers (#4087).

  • Breaking: [server.tls] takes the family keys: the table’s presence turns TLS on (enabled is gone), cert_file is certificate_file, reload_interval_secs is reload_interval_s (unset by default, where the files were read every 60 seconds; SIGHUP always reads them), and client_auth = "off" is "none". The chart’s config.server.tls follows, and an empty table means TLS off (#4087).

  • Breaking: [server.connection] is [server] header_read_timeout_ms (30000 by default, where the bound was 10 seconds, and 0 is refused); max_concurrent_streams and the HTTP/2 keep-alive keys are gone (#4087).

  • Breaking: ferroehr healthcheck asks GET /health/readiness on the server.listen port (over TLS with [server.tls] set) and exits 1 while the server drains, where it asked {rest root}/status; the reason on stderr reads healthcheck: unhealthy: …. GET /health answers the readiness status with {"state": …} and GET /health/liveness answers {"state":"up"}, where both answered a plain-text OK (#4087).

  • The request id is the server’s own, minted for every request and carried by the request log and the access record; a client’s X-Request-Id is returned to it unchanged and no longer recorded. A request past server.request_timeout_ms or over the body limit, a refused caller and a panicked handler answer the openEHR { error, message } body, and the panic message reaches neither the body nor the log. Responses are compressed at the default gzip and Brotli quality, from 1 KiB up (#4087).

  • The boot banner is the FerroHEALTH banner: the wordmark, the build line ferroehr <version> (<commit>), and the facts (manufacturer, profile, pins, support period, deployment) as one list, with the sandbox notice below (#4087).

  • Chart 19.0.0: config.server carries max_concurrent_requests and caller_rate, and config.rest the REST surface; the rendered ferroehr.toml changes accordingly (#4087).

  • Breaking: the usage report is sent by ferrohealth-usage-report 0.1.2 (#4087), the FerroHEALTH products’ shared reporter, on the same envelope v2. The status object loses spec_profile, and postgres_major is left out when the database does not answer. The daily metrics lose the aql group and the aql_executions and aql_slow counters, and gain the responses_4xx counter. Routes outside the API families (the health family, the management surface, the status and discovery documents) are counted in no group. A replica adds its counts to the shared window at its own daily attempt instead of every five minutes, and a daily report that does not reach the collector keeps its counts for the retry an hour later where it dropped them. A failed or refused send is logged at WARN where it was DEBUG, and the boot line takes the family’s wording. The clinical migration 0018_usage_report_envelope drops the slow column and the aql rows and adds usage_report_counter.

  • HTTP Basic credentials are cached for 300 seconds by default (#4088). [auth.basic] cache_ttl_seconds defaulted to 0, so every Basic request ran the Argon2id derivation, 10 to 15 ms of CPU, which capped the mixed ITS-REST and AQL workload against a release build on one host at 408 op/s; with the cache it reached 1559 op/s. ferrohealth-smart 0.7.5 makes 300 the default. Only a credential that verified is kept, under a keyed hash drawn at boot, and the cache empties at a restart. Set 0 to check every request. FerroEHR takes ferrohealth-smart 0.7.5, ferrohealth-authz 0.1.5, ihe-atna and ehds-logging 0.2.13 and ferrobridge-term 0.1.139. Helm chart 16.0.1 states the new default.

  • Three AQL shapes no longer read every composition (#4089, #4090), measured against a release build on one host holding about 51 000 compositions. A population query ordered by c/context/start_time/value with a small fetch reads the compositions in start-time order from a new index and stops at the limit: 169 ms became 7 ms at p50. A c/archetype_details/template_id/value predicate on a COMPOSITION reads the indexed template id of the version: 142 ms became 2 ms for a template nothing matches, and 29 ms became 11 ms for one of thirteen templates. A COMPOSITION, EHR_STATUS or EHR_ACCESS root is bound at its root row, so a containment with OR probes one row per version where it read every node of it. Clinical migration 0017 adds the index and the planner statistics, and analyzes the node table once.

  • The scheduled audit chain check verifies the records written since the last intact link (#4100). audit.verify_audit_chain_incremental() recomputes only the records after the checkpoint it keeps in audit.audit_chain_checkpoint, checks the chain head, and moves the checkpoint when it finds nothing: on 428,000 records a full pass took about 35 s, a run over the last 1,000 records 76 ms and one with nothing new 2 ms. A full pass runs every [audit.store] full_verify_interval_seconds (new, default one week, 0 for on demand only) and after any run that found damage, and SELECT * FROM audit.verify_audit_chain() stays the full pass on demand. With the cheaper run, verify_interval_seconds defaults to one hour, where it was one day. The chain digest is unchanged.

  • The FHIR Feed owes only the records written while it is configured (#4102). A record waiting for delivery is a row in audit.fhir_feed_outbox, which the store writes with the record while [audit.fhir_feed] is on and delivery removes. The two partial indexes over the unset delivery stamps, which held every record of a deployment without a sink (about 4.8 MB each at 428,000 records), are dropped; the syslog one served no query, since syslog delivers from its own spool. Records stored before this release and never delivered ship once a feed first runs.
